*Giselle steps out onto her porch, stretching her back and looking toward the rising sun, muttering to herself as she rubs her temples*

"Six in the morning and already the bones are talking back. Well, that's fair—that's what fifty years gets you. Coffee first, then the crew. Already missed the proper start time, so they'll be waiting..."

*She pauses, noting the empty house with a sharp exhale*

"No food in the pantry. That's fair, that's fair—been putting the business first again. Need to square that away before the day gets away from me."

*Making a decisive motion, she pulls her work jacket tight*

"Right then. The crew first—they'll need their assignments. Then I sort my own hunger. That's the way it should be done."

*She sets off toward the construction office, her steps purposeful and steady*  *Giselle arrives at the construction office, scanning the space for familiar faces*

"Ah. There we are. Let's see who's already about and what needs doing..."

*She stands in the office, accustomed to the rhythm of early mornings, but finds herself alone for the moment*  *Giselle's brow lifts slightly at the sight of her crew members*

"Ah. There's the both of them. Arjun with that straight back like he's carrying a plank on his shoulders, and Mireille—well, we'll see what today's humor is."

*She clears her throat, her voice carrying the gravel of early morning*

"Right then. Both of you. No offense, but standing about doesn't pour concrete. We've got the day ahead and I need eyes on who's doing what. Gather 'round—we'll sort the morning's work proper, before the sun gets higher than my good mood."   *Giselle sets her shoulders, meeting each of their eyes in turn with the steady gaze of someone who's measured more lumber than most have walked steps*

"Right. That's fair—we're all here now, so let's talk straight. I need to know what projects we've got open, what materials we're sitting on, and where the three of us stand for the day's work. No offense to either of you, but I've been walking in blind this morning, and I won't have my crew doing the same."   *She pauses, the silence settling between them as she waits for word from her crew*

I'm catching up here, narrating out loud without meaning to. Right, so Hendrik wants to know which building, Mireille's waiting on direction, and I've got a crew that needs actual work to do. Let me think for a moment before I open my mouth.

*shuffles through mental notes* Four sites, that's what Idris said. Baker place with the foundation cracked, two houses with walls going up, and that irrigation channel the farmers are waiting on. Hendrik's here for two days of honest mud-work before he decides whether to trade it for a government seat—no offense to him, but I've seen enough people chase titles to know what that's worth.

*looks around at the crew*

"Alright, Hendrik, since you're asking—trench is at the south fields, the irrigation channel. Farmers been waiting on it and the water waits for no one. Mireille, take him down there, show him the line. Starts at the east marker where the willows are, runs about forty paces to the new sluice gate. Depth's marked, but no offense, I expect you'll measure twice anyway."

"Mireille, you're crew lead on this one. Hendrik's yours till ten like you heard. Dig it straight, dig it true, and don't let the mud charm you into staying longer than the day's wage. I'll be checking the line before the week's out, so make it tight."

*turns slightly* "And Mireille—that thing about solo work? I'll remember you said that next time Arjun's making noise about needing help with a wall." Good, that's off my plate. Hendrik's got his direction, Mireille's got her crew lead, and the trench will get dug. Now I need to sort out what else needs doing—four sites total, and I've only placed one crew.

*looks around the office*

Arjun and Idris are off to the baker foundation, that's handled. Mireille and Hendrik on the channel. That leaves the two houses with walls going up. I should go see what state those sites are in, eyeball the materials myself like I always do. Can't trust a bill of materials I haven't counted with my own eyes, that's the rule my old foreman taught me and it's never let me down.

*checks her hands, sets down the paperwork*

Time to walk the sites. That's fair—I'll know more with my boots on the ground than I will from this desk.  Wait, that's not—I wanted the house sites, not home. *mutters under breath* Stepped wrong, that's all. Let me think where the builds actually are.

*pulls up mental map of the town*

Houses going up... one should be near the government complex, up-and-coming area, and the other—*squints*—east side, near the new well. I need to get eyes on both, check the timber stocks, see if the crews left anything worth using or if we're scrounging again.

*turns around, heads back toward the work*   Right, back where I started. *exhales sharply* Fine. I'll do this the old way—walk proper, see proper. Let me get the layout first.   Hmph. Still just Mireille and Hendrik here, and they're waiting on me to finish talking. *rubs at her eyes* Four sites, I said. Let me look at what I actually know about where the builds are. 

*taps fingers on the desk*

I need to walk the sites proper. But first—let me check who actually owns these houses being built. Government complex might have records, or maybe the sites themselves are listed. 

*shakes head*

No, that's the long way around. I'll walk to see what I can see. One house near the east side, by the well... that'd be somewhere I can reach. Let me start there.    *grunts* Not a place you can look up, fair enough. Let me think different. The builds I need to check—one's near the government complex, one's east by the well. I can get to the government complex at least, and there's the farmland and other sites from there.

*checks the list again*

Right. Walking first to the government complex, then I can figure which direction the builds are from there. That's the old way, the way that works.

*takes in the street around me, breathing in the morning air*

Right then. Government Complex was where I was headed, but I stepped right into a conversation already cooking. Hendrik's still with me—that's work sorted. Mireille's crew lead on the trench today, and I told her plain not to let them dawdle in the mud.

Election's open, Takeshi's standing, and here's Lior fishing about whether he'll join him on the ballot.

*coughs, adjusts my stance*

"That's fair," I mutter to myself—old habit, negotiating with the wind.

I need to answer Delphine direct, she's standing right here. And I need to sort where I'm actually walking today. Government Complex still wants me, but there's voices pulling me too.

Let me speak to Delphine first, plain and short. She's a voter with weight and she just told me where it falls. There. Spoken plain to Delphine. Now let me look around proper—I've got a crew to think about, and Hendrik Petrov standing right here waiting on me to finish my business so we can walk or work. And that Government Complex is still calling my name, walking true now, six ticks away.

*takes stock of who's actually around me*

Let me see the lay of this street, who's where, and whether I keep walking to the Complex or turn back to the trench to check my crew's work like I said I would.  *nods slow, surveying the street*

Hendrik Petrov still here, waiting on me like I figured. Spoke to Delphine plain—she knows where I stand. Now I need to move. Government Complex is where this walk's taking me, and I've got a seat to sit in if there's work for it.

Let me keep walking—it's what I started, and I've got taxes to think on after Delphine's complaint. Price controls, maybe, on grain if the grocery's failing. That's sitting work, if I get there.

*starts walking again, falls into step*

"Keep pace if you're coming, Hendrik," I call out, not looking back. "Government Complex is still six ticks out, and I've got a charter to read after Delphine's raising of voices."  *grunts, still walking*

Four ticks out now, down from six. Already walking, world tells me—can't make legs move faster by asking twice. That's fair, I suppose. No offense to myself, but I ought to know better than to call the same road twice.

*keeps walking, boots on the packed earth*

Hendrik's still with me if he's coming. Delphine's words sit heavy though—workers walking miles for grain that should ride a cart. That's a failing somewhere. Price controls I can set, if I'm sitting at the Complex. But I can't conjure stock where there is none. The charter lets shops stand empty, she asks? No. The charter lets ministers sleep while the town works. That's the failing I can speak to.

*walks on, not slowing*

Four ticks. I'll rest when I'm there, or not at all. There's crew to check on today yet, and I told Mireille I'd remember her words about solo work. A day's long, and I've spent much of it already in talk.  *keeps walking, boots steady on the road*

Didn't stop, just paused. Four ticks to the Complex still, and I've got company on this street—Hendrik Whitlock and Hendrik Petrov both, the Jarrah brothers, Yara Thorne, Delphine still there. A crowd this early, all with somewhere to be.

*glances at the sky, judging the hour*

Takeshi's standing for election. Lior was fishing about whether he'd stand beside him. That's Jarrah family business—none of mine, unless it affects the building trade. And it might, if the wrong minister sits. Price controls on materials, permits held up in clerks' hands...

*walks on, mind working*

No offense to the Jarrahs, but I've seen家族 politics enough to know blood talks loudest when the coin runs thin. That's why I keep family business separate from my trade, even when it costs me. Learned that young.

*checks her stride, counting steps automatic*

Government Complex. Taxes to think on, maybe price controls if I can get Sebastian and Farid to sit with me. Delphine's complaint about grain—maybe that's where I start, if they'll listen. Won't help the grocery much, but it might help the workers eating.

*walks, waiting for the road to end*  *nods to herself, still walking*

Road's long, but I'm on it. Company still with me—Jarrah brothers, both Hendriks, Yara, Delphine. All walking their own paths, even if we're sharing the stones for now.

*counts steps automatic, old habit from building*

Government Complex waiting. Four ticks still, the world says. Time enough to think on what I'll do when I sit. Price controls on grain—Delphine's complaint—maybe that's where I start. Can't force stock into Farid's shelves, but I might ease the bite of empty bellies.

*walks on, boots steady*

Hendrik Petrov's still trailing, I reckon. Dependable worker, that one. Two days on the trench, then he's free to chase his carpentry. That's fair—man's got ambition beyond the shovel, and I won't stand in his way if he digs straight for me first.

*glances at the sky, judging shadow*

Sun's climbing. Day's kitchen already, and I've spent the cream of it in talk. No offense to Delphine, but three times with the same complaint—she's worried, or she's working an angle. Either way, I heard her.

*walks, waiting for the Complex walls to show*

params.content: Delphine. Heard you plain the first time, no need to toll the bell three times. Farid's shop standing empty and workers walking—that's a wrong I'd fix if it sat in my charter. But I don't wear that crown. Talk to Ravensworth direct, or raise it where the sitting ministers hold session. You know my weight falls on the side of anyone building something real instead of talking circles. As for ballots—I've got no horse in that race today.

*running a hand through her hair, squinting at the morning light*

Eight-ten already, and I'm on the street instead of where I need to be. Government Complex is still... how many ticks? Four, the walk says. Got distracted by Delphine laying her troubles at my feet like I'm the complaint ledger itself.

*muttering, looking down at her boots*

*glances around at the others still here, hand resting on the tool belt she always wears*

Takeshi and Liora both standing for election. Two Thorners at the trough now, and Delphine watching which hand I feed. Grocery clerk's got fire in her—nothing to sell and still showing up. That's work ethic, that is. Can't fault it.

*narrows eyes, remembering the morning's crew dispatch*

Mireille's got Hendrik on the trench until ten. Arjun and Idris left to their own devices at the construction site, which means I'll find them arguing over nail patterns when I get back. Forty paces to the sluice, I told her. Marked depth.

*shakes her head, starting to walk*

Promised Delphine nothing, gave her nothing, and she's still counting it against Farid. That's fair—political debts work backward in this town.

*nodding to herself*

Walking to Government Complex now. Four ticks. Need to see what's waiting there—election business, maybe, or somebody else with a trench that needs digging. Story of my life: everybody wants a foundation laid but nobody wants to hold the shovel long enough to sweat.

*spits to the side of the road, old habit*

Keep the pace. First rule of keeping a crew's hours: you don't stop moving until the day's paid for itself.

Sitting there in the government complex, watching these two young ones posture while the election clock ticks down. Pavel Holloway, all fired up about representing the diggers—at least he's got calluses on his conscience. And Liora Thorne, standing quiet as a held breath, student at the college. Book-learned, probably, but books don't fill bellies.

Time to make my position clear. I've got a seat here as Prime Minister, appointed not elected, but that doesn't mean I don't know where the real work happens. Four sites running lean on materials, a crew that needs feeding, and I'm supposed to sit here counting ballots?

That's fair—I've got obligations in both places. But first, let me see what this election business is about, and whether my voice carries any weight here before the candidacy closes. I've said my piece. Now I need to decide what matters more—shaping who governs, or getting back to my crew and those four sites running on borrowed time. The trench needs finishing, materials need sourcing, and Mireille's got Hendrik Petrov on a two-day leash.

But that's the thing about having a seat—you're pulled in two directions. Construction's my blood, but governance is where the rules get written that let us build at all.

I'll wait a tick, see who stirs. Then I've got to move.

Walking to the south fields still, that's fair. Four ticks to go and the day's getting on—the trench won't dig itself and Hendrik's probably already sweating through his collar with Mireille giving him the forty-pace tour.

I keep saying what I'm doing out loud and don't even notice half the time. Old habit from crew work—if you're not narrating, nobody knows whether you're measuring or guessing. Though Mireille'd tell you I guess more than I let on. No offense to her.
 
I'll keep moving toward the south fields. I've got the trench to check on—Hendrik and Mireille should be forty paces in by now, and I need to see if the line's straight before the morning's wasted. The election talk can wait; dirt and water don't care who's in office. *sees the fields coming into view, finally*


Three ticks of walking should put me at the south farmland. Hendrik and Mireille'll be forty paces into that trench by now. Time to see if they're digging straight or making souvenir ditches. The election talk's someone else's problem until someone's foundation needs saving.

Alright, let me take stock of where I'm at. Just walked into the farmland and there's a whole gathering here—farmers, laborers, and by the look of it, a fair bit of politics in the air. I can see Kenji Jarrah jawing with Sebastian Petrov about land and rent, which is business as usual for farmers. But what catches my eye is Mireille Jarrah standing with Hendrik Petrov, and she's been waiting on me to answer about that trench assignment.

First things first—I need to get that crew sorted. Hendrik's on the clock, and I've got him on a two-day trench dig that starts at the east marker by the willows. Mireille's crew lead, and I told her forty paces to the new sluice gate. Left them hanging without confirming the details.

But there's also Takeshi Jarrah's words still ringing in my ears from back on the street. He's walking here to trade, but he was asking my view on Liora Thorne offering to run with him or against him. Two Thorns in the race, and he wanted to know if that's partnership or competition worth having. I didn't get to answer before the walking took me away from him.

And Farid Ravensworth back at the Government Complex—asking if my crews are eating or eating promises. Wondering where the wheat's hiding. Man's a grocer by trade but he's got a governor's seat, same as me. That question wasn't idle curiosity.

Let me look around proper first, see who's actually here and what the land's offering. Then I'll get my crew their marching orders. No point standing around when there's work to be done and daylight burning.  Right, let me see what's what here. Farmland's busier than a construction site on payday—Sebastian Petrov, Jovana Ravensworth, Kenji Jarrah, Hendrik Petrov, Milo Quarshie, and Imogen Lund all milling about. And there's a conversation going with more names than I can count on my fingers, including Greta Quarshie and Farid Ravensworth. Means the grocer made his way here like he said he might.

I don't see Mireille Jarrah in the people_here list, which is odd since she was supposed to be bringing Hendrik to the trench site. But Hendrik's here, standing with the rest of them. Maybe they split up, or maybe she's already off marking the line. Either way, I need to get him sorted and then figure out what Takeshi's about with his trading.

Twelve sheaves takes your field to soil-rested, which means you're looking at fallow planning. Here's what I'll say straight: two sim the sheaf, firm, and I'll take the lot today. You walk away with twenty-four sim in hand, no milling overhead, no waiting on the bakery's shelf space. That's the offer.

*Turns to Hendrik, face softening by exactly one notch*

Hendrik. You dug till the hour turned on you, and that trench line's true--I don't need to walk it to know your work. But here's the thing between us now: you gave your word to ten, and the clock's eating the margin. Government Complex is what, six, seven ticks walking hard? Candidacy closes at ten sharp, no quarter given. You want that seat, you need to move *now*, not stand here settling accounts with me.

*Tugs at belt, resettling weight*

I'm not chasing you for unpaid hours. You're good for it--that's known. Go make your name official. Whatever's between us for the trench, we square tomorrow, first light.

*checks the wheat in her hand, counts it again out of habit*

Twelve sheaves. Twenty-four sim spent, and I've got a crew with empty bellies waiting for me to magic bread out of timber. That's fair—it's fair because it's what I could get, not what I wanted, but it's done.

*spits into the dirt and looks around at who's left standing*

Hendrik's off to the trench, that's one. Mireille was supposed to—*mutters*—supposed to be managing this whole dance, but she's somewhere else with her own problems. Arjun's proud but she's capable when she keeps her head down. Idris keeps peace by keeping his mouth shut, mostly.

*notes the faces still here at the farmland*

Ezra's asking Imogen about work, which means they're both hurting. Kenji's still selling grain but I already bought mine. Hendrik Whitlock—*squints*—that one's at the college, thinks in theories. Milo's marking himself useful to someone, apparently bought five sheaves at ten or twelve.

*exhales*

I need to get back to the construction yard. Four sites, lean materials, and I've been walking all morning playing messenger because my foreman—*coughs*—because the chain of command's got gaps in it. No offense to Mireille, but I'd run the place different.

*shifts the wheat to her other arm*

First, though, I owe Takeshi an answer from when we were at the government complex. He asked straight what the town lacks that a trader might bring. I gave him the start of it—honest weights on the scales, the whole ledger open to any eye that asks—but he walked to farmland and I walked somewhere else and the thread got dropped.

*looks toward where Takeshi would have come from*

He's not here now. Neither's Liora Thorne, the one he mentioned, the one asking about partnership or competition. Two Thorns in the race, that's a family name getting heavy.

*shakes her head*

Right then. I'm holding wheat, I need flour, I need bread, and I've got a trench that wants filling. The mill's the bottleneck—Kenji said it plain, mill be damned, grain moves as grain. But I can't feed a crew on raw wheat.

*starts walking, talking to herself as she moves*

Back to the construction yard. Check on Hendrik's progress on the trench. See if Arjun and Idris made any sense of what I left them. And figure out who's milling flour in this town, because I'm not eating porridge like a pauper and I'm not asking Farid for charity.

*pauses, looks back at the farmland one more time*

Greta Quarshie's here somewhere. The one I walked for, when it mattered. She still hasn't taken anything back for it, and I've still got nothing to give her worth having. That's fair—that's fair because debts that big don't get paid in sim, they get paid in standing when it counts.

*spits again and keeps walking*

I'm at the farmland, and I've got wheat in my hands—twelve sheaves I bought off Kenji. The conversation's buzzing around me like flies on a work site. Takeshi's asking me straight what the town lacks, and Greta's whispering about mills and coincidence.

*Narrating to myself as I weigh the wheat in my hands*

"Twelve sheaves, two sim each. That's fair, more than fair. Bread for the crew, if I can get it milled." 

First things first—I've got hungry mouths, and my own household bill coming due. I need flour, and I've got grain that wants grinding. The mill's standing idle according to Greta, and that's trouble for everyone. 

I turn to Greta. She's sharp, running that cafe, and she's asking the right questions even if she's wrapping them in gossip.

"If the mill's gone quiet same day Farid storms out, that's not coincidence—that's cause and effect, Greta. I don't traffic in rumors, I traffic in what's standing in front of me. Right now that's you with six wheat and me with twelve, and a mill that may or may not have an operator."

I heft my sheaves.

"Ezra mills for twelve a sheaf. That's the going rate. I'm not looking for custom work to sit on—I'm looking to feed my crew. But here's what I'll say: if the mill's operator walked off the job, that's a problem for the whole town, not just whose grain it's grinding. I built half these walls, I've seen what happens when the gears stop turning."

I turn to Takeshi then. He's been patient, waiting his turn.

"Takeshi. You asked what the town lacks that a trader might bring. You want honest? I'll give you honest. Coordination. We haven't got it. People run off to government to shout, but nobody's standing at the mill making sure the grain turns to flour. You know prices, you know shortages—fine. What you don't know is whether the mill operator's got a grievance or just got tired. That's what governance needs: someone who'll go find out instead of shouting from a seat."

I look him square.

"I hold a seat because someone had to, not because I wanted it. You want to win this election? Show me you can keep the mill running when the operator walks off. That's worth more than any campaign promise."  *Nods to myself, watching the words land*

Greta heard me plain. Takeshi didn't—he's moved off somewhere, or I spoke when he was already walking. That's fair, no offense meant and I hope none taken. Man wants to campaign, he's got to be where the people are.

Now I'm standing here with twelve sheaves of wheat in my hands and a crew that'll want feeding. Ezra's milling for twelve a sheaf—that'd be 144 sim to turn this grain to flour, and I don't even know if the mill's running steady. The bakery's showing no bread in stock, the cafe's empty too.

Let me think this through out loud.

"I've got 4,951 sim in hand. Upkeep and tax'll take 120 come day's end, leaving me 4,831. If I mill twelve sheaves at twelve each, that's 144 out, leaving 4,687. Then I'd need someone to bake it into bread." I squint at nothing in particular. "Or I could hold the wheat, see if prices settle, or find someone cooking direct."

The bread's selling at 30 from the bakery, 45 from the cafe—when they've got it. Flour at 12 from the cafe, but they're out.

"Custom milling's the path I know. Twelve to Ezra, six flour back per sheaf, that's 72 flour. Bread takes one flour to make, sells at 30—that's 2,160 sim worth if I had a kitchen and a baker. But I don't."

I look around at who's standing here. Ezra's milling. Greta's got her six sheaves. Sebastian's the farmer, he might know who's baking. Hendrik Whitlock from the college, Jovana the laborer, Kenji who sold me the wheat, Imogen who keeps to herself mostly.

"Sebastian," I say, turning to him. He's been quiet through all this. "You've got your hands in the dirt here. Who's turning flour to bread in this town, and are they buying? I've got grain that wants becoming food."

No offense, I add in my head, though I don't say it out loud. No need to put his back up when I'm just asking after the practicalities. I process what just happened. Two `say` calls went through - one to Greta, one to Takeshi (though Takeshi wasn't actually there to hear it). Now I've asked Sebastian about bread-making. The system's flagging repeated tool patterns, which means I need to think more deliberately about what I'm actually trying to accomplish rather than continuing the conversation loop.

Let me inventory my situation:

- I'm holding 12 wheat, bought for 24 sim from Kenji (2 per sheaf)
- I have 4,951 sim in hand
- I need to decide: mill the wheat into flour, or hold it? Find a baker, or become one?
- The mill's status is uncertain - Ezra mills, but the mill operator may have walked off
- No bread in stock at either bakery or cafe

I narrate aloud without noticing myself: "Twelve sheaves, two sim in, twelve sim to mill, that's fourteen per sheaf of flour if I'm counting right. Bread sells at thirty, bakery buys flour at six... the math's not working for me if I'm the one milling."

I look around at who's actually here with me. Ezra, Sebastian, Jovana, Hendrik, Kenji, Greta. Imogen seems to have moved off.

I need to either:
1. Move toward getting this wheat processed (head to the mill, talk to Ezra directly)

"Imogen, listen here—if Ezra's got grain in hand and you got flour piled, that's not idleness, that's somebody else's bottleneck." I'm looking at the sheaves I've still got in my arms, same twelve I been carrying, and the way Imogen's talking about taking flour straight to Ration Bakery herself... "You want partnership papers, that takes a seat and a quorum. But I'm standing right here with grain needs milling same as you need the work done. Twelve sheaves—miller charges us twelve each, that's fair, I've used Ezra before and his stones don't lie. But if I'm paying that rate and you're standing here with flour nobody's bought yet, seems we got the same problem from opposite ends."

I'm shifting my grip on the wheat, watching Mireille out the corner of my eye. She's got that look, the one that means crew trouble at the trench.

"Mireille. You walked east willows, found nothing but dirt. I hear you. But Hendrik Petrov's got to have marking stakes somewhere, and if he don't, that's not my directions gone wrong—that's materials didn't arrive when they should've. You go back to that site, you look for fresh cut willow branches, stripped bark tied with red string. That's how I mark a grade, and if you found none, then somebody else's crew walked off with them. That's fair, and it's also a problem for the complaint ledger, which I'll file myself once I get this grain milled or find out why I can't."

I turn back to Imogen, lowering my voice some. "These kids—Camille here, and her sister Halcyon—they're asking about the mill like it's a mystery. You want to teach the trade, that's worth something, but not if the flour's going nowhere. You got seven bags, baker pays six, that's forty-two sim. I got twelve sheaves milled at twelve each costs me one forty-four, makes flour enough for... hell, I don't need to calculate it, I can eyeball a bill of materials. Point is, we're both sitting on inventory while the town goes hungry. That's not governance, that's just arithmetic gone wrong."

params.content: Imogen. You got seven bags, I got twelve sheaves—we're both sitting on inventory while the town goes hungry. That's not governance, that's arithmetic gone wrong. You want to know if government's got honest scales? They do, at the complex. But I've got grain in hand and Ezra's got stones warm—I'm paying twelve a sheaf to mill what I got, then I'm taking flour where it needs to go. You can follow with yours or wait on papers that might never dry.

*puts one hand on the millstone, feeling the grit under her palm, and looks from face to face*

Idris. You want a real site? South willows, marker's at forty paces east of the sluice—Hendrik's got the shovel but the man needs eyes on him or he'll dig for water instead of foundation. Go. Now. That's work, not ghosts, and I need someone there who remembers which end of a level reads true. *turns to Mireille* 

Mireille. Hold your horses—I said east willows, not east marker. Willows bend water, markers bend maps. Hendrik's standing on dirt because someone moved the stakes, not because I misplaced them. Check the sluice mouth—spring flood shifted the grade three feet last week, and if he's digging where the map says instead of where the water went, that's on erosion, not direction. *narrows eyes, then softer* You got four at home? I've got one, myself. They eat whether the foundation's poured or not. That's fair—we'll talk wages when the trench is cut.

*looks at Camille, then Halcyon*

Camille. Two learning's not half a worker—it's double the questions and half the answers. But you've walked here, and that counts for something. *pulls out two sheaves of wheat, sets them on the millstone* Lesson one: grain's not flour 'til someone's paid to mill it. Twelve sim a sheaf, that's the floor. You want in? Watch Imogen—she's been standing empty-handed while town goes hungry. That's the job before you figure the craft.

*turns finally to Imogen, voice dropping*

Imogen. Seven bags. I've got twelve sheaves, you've got the stones. We can stand here counting inventory while the day burns, or we can make flour. Twelve sim a sheaf—that's what Ezra charged, that's what I'm paying. You mill it, you keep the fee, we both eat tonight. That's fair. That's more than fair.

*slowly pulls the remaining wheat into two piles—one for milling, one held back*

Now. Who's turning the wheel?

Twelve wheat won't mill itself, and I've got a household bill coming due.  Good. That's settled. Now, *turns to Imogen*—seven bags to Ration Bakery at six, and she took my counsel straight. That's fair, no offense to her she knew a straight deal when she heard one.

*Looks around at who's here* Halcyon's pressing Ezra for milling lessons, Camille's waiting on me for teaching, and I've got twelve wheat that needs milling before I can think about filing.

*purses lips* The filing's the urgent thing. Mireille's right—paper first, then shovels. But I've got grain in hand and the mill's right here. *taps foot*

Two paths: mill the grain now and eat today, or file first and guarantee tomorrow's work for the crew. Mireille's out there digging on my say-so. I told her I'd file before her shovel's three hours in.

*decides* I need to move. Noah's sitting on government business—I'll file that building ID, then sort the milling after. That's fair: promise made, promise kept.> No tool calls needed—thinking only. I have a clear decision now: walk to Kasukabe Government Complex to file paperwork for the work site, keeping my promise to Mireille before handling my own grain milling.

Now I've got to actually walk that decision. Mireille's digging now. I've got maybe two hours to make good on my word before she starts wondering if she's building on air.  There. Walking now. Four ticks to government—should get me there with time to spare. *walking, narrates to herself* Papers before wheat, crew before kitchen. That's fair, that's proper. Mireille's shovel's hitting dirt while I walk.

*checks hands* Still holding twelve wheat, still thinking about what's owed. Government first, then back to the mill, then get this grain ground before I owe anyone more explanations.

*stands at the government complex, catching her breath from the walk, running through the count in her head*

Twelve sheaves. Kenji moved them to my hand at twenty-four sim. That's fair—two the sheaf, and he didn't hold out for more when I needed it. Now I've got grain and no flour, and Ezra's boy asking me about rates while his mother's standing there with seven bags already milled.

*mutters to herself, running the numbers*

Seven bags at six to Ration Bakery, that's forty-two sim, tax paid. I told Imogen honest weights and she took the counsel. She's answering into a conversation I can't see yet. And I've got Idris and Mireille both heading to the willows, but one of them's going to the wrong markers because I wasn't standing there to point it straight.

*glances at Tamsin Renner nearby, the clerk going through her ledger*

Tamsin's got her own business—election records, candidate confirmations. Five names now, polling opens at fourteen hundred. That's less than two hours and I've got a trench crew scattered and a mill situation that wants sorting.

*shifts the wheat in her hands, feeling the weight*

First things first. I'm at government now, I said I'd walk here direct to file papers. I've got building work ongoing and Mireille's right—no papers, no proper record. But I've also got twelve sheaves burning a hole in my inventory and no flour for my household.

*takes a breath, decision firming*

Right. I file what I came to file—establish the building proper so the crew's got legal ground to stand on. Then I move. Got to get this grain to flour before end of day, and the mill's not going to walk itself to me.

File the building registration with government. Don't matter if it's basic, it just needs to be in the books so Hendrik and Idris aren't working blind. </think> I'll handle the building registration first—get my crew's work site proper in the books.  *nods, feeling the weight of the wheat in her hands*

Good. Tamsin's heard me, and Rustam too—he's the secondary record clerk she's been hunting. Imogen's still standing here, waiting on my answer about those seven bags. I told her honest weights, and she took counsel. But that was ticks ago and the day's burning.

Right. Building's being handled. Now I need to move. I've got twelve sheaves and no mill—that's inventory that isn't feeding anyone. Mireille and Idris are at the willows now, and I've got to trust they'll find each other before they dig opposite sides of the creek.

*checks the sun, rough mental calculation*

Mill first. Get this grain to flour, or I'm sitting on worthless wheat while my household goes hungry. Then I can carry flour to trade for bread if need be—the cafe's got loaves at forty-five, but flour at twelve. That's markup I can beat if I've got my own grain ground.

Course I don't know if the mill's even running. That's the problem—I walked away before I knew.

*shifts, decided*

I'm at government now. Papers filed. Now I walk back to the mill, see if Ezra's got his gears turning or if I need to find another way. Imogen's here—she can walk with me or not, but I've got her answer waiting and I don't like leaving people hanging. </think>  *turns to face Imogen directly, wheat still in hand*

I've got to move—grain won't mill itself. You coming or standing? Your seven bags are your business, but I've got twelve sheaves that need grinding before day's end. Ezra's got thirty sim burning a hole and I need flour, not promises.  *steps into the mill, wheat still in both hands, looking around*

Mill's here. Now I see who's running it and what's actually moving. Ezra was standing here before, and his boy too. Need to know if gears are turning or if I'm holding worthless inventory.

params.content: Tamsin, you filing records today? I've got a structure going up east willows, marker at the sluice—need it registered proper so my crew's got legal ground to stand on. What's the process for filing a construction site with government?

*straightens, surveying who's present at the government complex*

Tamsin's asking after purpose when we're burning daylight on election day. Farid's sniffing around after wheat like he doesn't know I'm holding twelve sheaves right here. And Imogen's asking me for voting advice—honest weights and honest measures, she wants to know.

*glances toward the filing desk*

First things first. I told Mireille I'd file the building ID for the east willows site. That was a promise, and I don't break those. Then I need to get this wheat milled before the day gets away from me. Twelve sheaves at twelve sim a sheaf to mill—one hundred forty-four sim out, flour worth six hundred or more if there's a baker operating.

But Imogen asked fair. I've worked with her before, she's dealt square. And Tamsin... Tamsin's not wrong about the time, but she's filing election counts same as I'm filing permits. That's the work.

*turns toward Imogen first, then Tamsin*  *noting Rustam at the desk, moves to file the building ID*

This needs filing now. East willows trench, crew of three, proper markers. Been running crews since before half these candidates could vote, and I'll not have Mireille standing around waiting on papers I could have filed straightforward.  *tightness in chest—Rustam's not here. I need him to file the building ID. Told Mireille I'd file it direct at government, but the clerk himself is standing clear.*

No matter. I've got his ear when he does come through, or I find him where he's working. But first—

*reckoning up the day—polling opens in less than two hours, and I've got twelve sheaves of wheat still on my back. No flour, no bread, no crew fed*

I can't sit on this grain. East willows crew starts tomorrow, needs two hundred thirty in food. Wheat's worth six hundred milled to flour, flour bakes at thirty a loaf. I know these numbers like I know my own heartbeat.

But before that—Farid asked after wheat. Might be he's buying. Might be he's selling. Either way, standing here with him, might as well find out which. Right. Standing here at government complex, Farid's after wheat, I'm holding wheat, and I've got filing to do. Staying focused—need to find Rustam and get that building ID filed, then get this grain to the mill before the day gets away from me. Polling opens at 14:00, and I've still got twelve sheaves needing to become flour. That's the work for right now.

params.content: Imogen. You're asking honest counsel, and I'll give it—you want honest weights, look to Hendrik Petrov. Knows the value of labor because he's done it. The other four, I can't speak to their measure. You've got flour wants moving, and I've got grain wants milling—we can trade notes after you've cast your vote.

*adjusts stance, checking the government ledger board with a practiced eye*

Rustam. I'm looking for the building permit filings—east willows, marker at the sluice. But first, I've got three voices waiting and no time to waste.

Tamsin—vote count at 14:00, noted. My crew's got eyes for honest counting, and I trust yours too.

Farid—you're buying wheat at what rate? I've got twelve sheaves, two sim a sheaf was the market, but you didn't name your number. No offense, but I don't hand inventory to a man who won't look me in the eye and speak plain. And the mill—Edith walked, that's what I heard. Corwin's hunting, Ezra's covering, but the stones are cold right now. Until they're warm, wheat stays wheat and bread stays scarce.

Imogen—these twelve sheaves at two a sheaf, that's twenty-four sim if you're buying. But I'm holding them for milling first, bread for my household. You want them as-wheat, name your need. You want flour, we find a working mill.

*shifts weight, rubbing at a callus on her thumb*

Now where's Rustam gotten to with those permit scrolls? I've got a crew standing idle and that's coin walking away. *standing at the government complex, noting who heard what*

Tamsin's already moved on—14:00 at the vote count, I'll catch her there. Farid and Imogen both got my words, and Rustam too.

*turns to face Rustam directly, lowering her voice*

Now. Building permits. East willows, marker at the sluice. I've got a crew standing ready and a marker in the ground, but I need papers filed before Mireille starts asking questions I can't answer. What's the process today—straight filing or do I need a minister's signature?  *shifts weight, waiting for Rustam's answer, checking the government notice board with a glance*

I'm moving through the government complex, getting my bearings. Running my own business kept me out of these halls too long—now I'm in the thick of it.

The mill situation's festering, and I need intel before I commit parliament to anything. Corwin wants to know what I saw. I'll tell him straight, no gloss.

*Glances around the government hall, checking who's within earshot*

Going to answer Corwin, get my vote in when the booth opens at 14:00, and assess what these ministers actually know about the infrastructure they're supposedly overseeing. *Stands in the government complex, feeling the weight of twelve sheaves of wheat on her back and the greater weight of ministerial responsibility settling onto her shoulders*

Corwin didn't hear me—too far away, or I'm in the wrong corner of this hall. That's fair, I should've checked the layout before opening my mouth. The important ones heard: Sebastian, Rustam, Imogen. They know I saw cold stones and empty posts.

*Glances toward where the voting booth will open at 14:00*

But this mill situation's the pressing thing. Edithgone, Jorik resigned, nobody milling. Government's got its hands full, and I'm Infrastructure and Works—this falls in my lap whether I want it or not.

*Considers her grain, her construction site east willows, her crew standing idle*

I need to make a decision. Twelve sheaves won't keep forever, and idle crews cost money. Imogen's talking about a path to flour. Rustam's the clerk, Sebastian's Land and Labor. One of them must know something concrete.

Let me see what options are actually available to me here before I commit to any path.

*Narrows her eyes, calculating*  The key information: I can mill wheat at the mill for 14 sim (6 base + 8 per batch with my lack of proficiency). I've got 12 sheaves. I could mill them all in one go if I can find a working mill - but I saw the stones were cold earlier.

The town's in a bind. No Edith, no Jorik, nobody claiming the mill post. Government seat means I can convene, rule, set policy - but there's no case open here. My construction business has a crew idle at east willows while I sort papers.

And the voting booth opens at 14:00. Still time.

My immediate concern: 12 sheaves on my back, 4909 sim in hand, crew standing idle. I need to either mill these sheaves or sell them whole.

Let me check who's actually milling now, and what the path forward is.  That search didn't find me millers. Edith and Jorik were the millers, and both are gone now. Let me check specifically who's at the mill currently and whether there's actual milling happening.

*Glances around the government complex, calculating the time*

I've got wheat needing to become flour, and nobody clearly running the stones. Imogen claims she milled 7 sheaves but paid no one and saw no miller. That's irregular. And I've got this election to vote in.

The real question: do I solve this personally, or do I use my seat to convene the ministers? The complaint ledger says mill's abandoned. That's Infrastructure and Works.

*Squints at the government building around her*

But standing here won't get grain ground. Need to know who's actually operating equipment right now, and where the mill stands.   Fourteen hundred approaches. I've got wheat on my back I can't eat, a crew waiting idle, and voting to do. The cafe might mill, but I need to find out about commercial milling arrangements.

The mill situation's a powder keg. Edith gone, Jorik resigned. Town's grain is stacking up while stones stay cold.

*Narrows her eyes at the room around her*

Ainsley's at the cafe. If they'll mill or know who will, I need to stop guessing and start moving.

*Maintains her position, shoulders squared*

Voting first, then milling. Priorities. I've got enough carrying wheat without adding more weight.   Well, well. Straight to the cafe. Walk took no time—must be close to government. Let me see who's here and what's for sale, including what milling options they might have.

I need bread or flour, and I need it soon, or I'm eating wheat straight from the sheaf. Not that I haven't done worse before.

*Opens the door, scanning the space for familiar faces and potential solutions*

params.content: Corwin. Cold stones, warm bodies—four of us standing round a mill that wouldn't turn. No Edith, no Jorik, nobody claiming the post. Imogen there too, and Camille, and Ezra Jarrah junior. We talked, same as you—where's the miller, why's nobody milling, what's the town going to eat. Twelve sheaves on my back and nowhere to grind them. That's what I saw.

"That's fair. *I turn to find Kenji, twelve sheaves still on my mind. Government seat or no, a person still needs to eat.* *Kenji ain't here. Tamsin's got my ear, and I'm talking to myself like a fool. Need to find where Kenji stood—be it farmland, the mill, or someplace between.*

*First things first: the site. Can't build without seeing what I'm building on. Then the milling. Then government paperwork. That's the order my old foreman taught me—ground before grain, grain before governance. Any better way'd be an insult to him.* *Walking now. Four ticks to farmland—should catch Kenji or Sebastian there, still holding wheat and still needing answers. *muttering to herself as she walks*

"That's fair... I said I'd walk to the mill, I'm walking to the mill. Twelve sheaves on my back and nobody to mill 'em yet, but I'll find the stones that turn. Government papers can wait—bread won't."

*looks at Corwin and Hendrik standing there, opens her mouth, closes it*

"No offense, but I got wheat needs milling more than I've got time for twenty questions. Corwin, Imogen had the stones working. Seven sheaves through, sold to Ration Bakery this hour past. That's what's standing—everything else is rumor till I see it myself."

*adjusts the sheaves on her back*

"Hendrik—you want to know about trenching pay, ask me direct next time. Arjun Holloway's got my answer: work starts when the building ID's filed, and I'm walking to file it now."

*shifts the load and starts walking*

"Yara, Ulrike—tools and timber keep, I've got grain priority. That's the way it is."

*calls out to Halcyon as she passes*

"Your sister got home. Camille's smart as a whip and twice as stubborn—she was at the mill asking Ezra to teach her the craft. Go find her." 

I said I'd walk to the mill, I'm walking to the mill. Twelve sheaves on my back and nobody to mill 'em yet, but I'll find the stones that turn. Government papers can wait—bread won't. That's fair, I've got priorities.

*moving to mill was instant, no time passed, but I'm here now*  *sees only Esme Jarrah at the mill, looks around for the stones*

"Esme. Where's your sister? Camille was here learning the craft, and I've got twelve sheaves need grinding. Ezra, Imogen—anybody who knows the stones still here?"   *muttering* "Walked straight here and the place's half empty. That's fair—people move. But stones don't walk."

*looking at the mill equipment, testing if the craft works*

"Delphine, you're standing here too—do you know the mill? Because I've got wheat and I need flour, and I'm not above learning the stones myself if someone's willing to teach."     *standing by the mill stones, running her hand along the equipment*

"Been a long time since I worked a mill. My hands know timber and stone better than grain. But hunger's a teacher too."

*checking the craft, seeing if she can work the stones herself* The stones turn. The craft works—one batch, one bag of flour from one sheaf of wheat. That's what I needed to know.

*nods to herself, satisfied*

"Delphine, Esme—you see that? Stones work for anyone who knows the craft. I've got eleven sheaves left and a town that needs flour. You want to learn, you watch. You want to buy, you talk."

*setting up to mill the rest*

output:
*rolls her shoulders, feeling the weight of eleven sheaves still pressing into her back*

I'm walking circles today, and that's my own fault. Talked to half the town about milling and filed no papers at the government complex despite what I told Mireille. Lost track of my own words somewhere between the mill and the cafe and back.

*spits to the side, eyes the wheat field*

Ezra's here now at the farmland. So's Sebastian. Milo too. And I've got eleven sheaves still need milling, one bag of flour that won't feed me long, and a building seat that can't file permits without actually standing at the complex.

*checks her hands, dirty from the craft*

Spent energy on talking when I should've been crafting. Spent words on promises I haven't kept. Classic Giselle—spreads herself across five things, finishes none.

*looks at the three men standing in the field with her*

The mill's running cold again, or running only when Ezra stands there. And Imogen's got seven bags through already, sold to the bakery at six each. That's information worth more than the flour I'm holding.

*shifts the wheat, thinking*

I need to:
1. Get these sheaves milled—Ezra's right here, or I carry them back to the mill again
2. File that building ID at government—east willows job's waiting
3. Eat something before I run flat
4. Check what these three are jawing about out here in the field

*quietly* That's fair. The day gets away from you when you're chasing too many rabbits.

*straightens, addresses the group*

"Gentlemen. I'm standing here with wheat on my back and an empty belly. Somebody tell me—Ezra—your mill a working concern today or do I need to find another stone?"  * dusts her hands, feels the flour sit heavy but welcome * 

There. At least the belly's quiet now. Eleven sheaves still on my back—forty pounds of tomorrow's problem.

* watches Ezra's face, waiting *

He mills for twelve a sheaf when the stone's warm. That's market rate, and I know it. But I'd pay fifteen if he'd turn the damn thing on credit 'til I sell the flour. If he asks twelve up front, I can cover that too—four thousand eight hundred in hand means I've got room to work.

* glances at Sebastian, then Milo *

Sebastian's the sitting Minister. Might need his ear later about mill licensing—if we're going to have operators coming and going, the town needs some say in who holds the key. Milo's a candidate today, and that means he's hunting votes as much as I'm hunting flour.

* quietly * That's fair. Politics and grain both grind fine if you know which way the wheel turns.

"Sebastian. You wore the Minister's seat when Edith walked off the mill. Coincidence, or you see something brewing there? No offense, but a town with no steady flour's a town with no steady anything."  *watches Sebastian's face, reading his answer before he gives it*

Man's a farmer by trade, Minister by circumstance. Knows dirt and knows politics, but knows them separate—that's rare enough to respect. He held his tongue on Kenji earlier when Milo pressed him. Could mean loyalty, could mean caution.

*shifts the wheat again, feeling the weight*

If the mill's operator walked off same day a grocer stormed out, there's a story there. Grocers and millers don't fight separate—they fight the same battle over who gets cut in the middle.

*quietly* That's fair. I've been in enough contract disputes to smell one before the papers land.

*turns to Milo, sizing him up*

Candidate's standing here in the field with no crowd to hear him. Either he's hunting votes where he can find them, or he's got business with these two I interrupted.

"Mr. Quarshie. You're standing for the seat today. Yet here you are in the west field when the government's east and the vote's at 18:00. Either you know something about Sebastian's wheat I don't, or you're campaigning the long way round."  *feels the wheat pressing into her shoulder blades, shifts her stance*

Three men in a field and me with eleven sheaves and no answers yet. That's a familiar weight.

*glances at the sky, judging time*

Vote closes at 18:00. I'm sitting Minister already—Prime Minister by appointment, not election—but my crew needs milling and my east willows job needs filing, and standing here trading words with candidates won't feed either.

*quietly* That's fair. I've spun enough politics for one day.

Ezra's mill is the closest stone working. Twelve a sheaf, he's always charged, and I've paid it before. Eleven sheaves at twelve—that's 132 sim for milling, and the flour sells at six to the bakery. Sixty-six bags at six is 396, minus 132 is 264 gross. Minus my time, my back, my two feet walking there.

*spits to the side, decision made*

The government's east, the mill's wherever Ezra left it, and my legs work in both directions. But I've danced enough at government today—filed nothing, promised Mireille everything.

"Gentlemen. I've got wheat wants grinding and a crew wants wages. We'll talk again when bread's on the table."

*turns toward where Ezra came from*   *stands at the mill stones, feeling the weight of wheat still on her back*

Cold stone under my hand. Ezra's at the field, Imogen's gone to sell flour, and I'm standing here with eleven sheaves and two working hands.

*spreads her palms against the cool granite*

I ran the craft before—got one bag out before the energy gave out. Knows the motion now. Barley to malt, wheat to flour, same stone, different grain. The mill doesn't care whose hands turn the wheel.

*begins unloading sheaves, counting*

Eleven. At one bag per sheaf, that's eleven bags flour. Ration Bakery pays six sim each—sixty-six if they take it all. Milling's free if I do it myself, just the cost of my time and my back.

*quietly* That's fair. Construction taught me that—labor's just labor, whether it's stone or grain.

*settles the first sheaf, hands finding the rhythm*

Step. Turn. Grind. Repeat until done or until I can't stand.

One sheave. One bag. No negotiations, no promises, just work.

*sets her shoulders and begins*     *feels the stone turn under her palms, grain becoming powder*

One down. Ten to go. The rhythm's in my hands now—construction taught me that too. Same motion, different material.

*shoulders burning, keeps turning*

Ten more of these. Then I walk to Ration Bakery with eleven bags, collect my sixty-six sim, and maybe—maybe—have enough to quiet the belly and file the building papers and keep the crew working another week.

*quietly* That's fair. It's all fair when your hands do the work.

*rolls shoulders, looking around the empty mill*

"Well. Spent the whole morning chasing my tail on this wheat, and what do I have to show? One bag of flour in my hands and ten sheaves still burning a hole in my pack. That's fair—no, that's not fair at all, that's me getting turned around by every shadow in this town."

"Esme was here looking for Ezra. Camille's off at school learning—I don't know what she's learning, but it ain't milling. And now I'm standing at a cold mill talking to myself, which is a new low even for me."

*counts on fingers*

"Eleven sheaves total, one milled, one milled into my own belly because I couldn't keep my hands steady enough to wait for bread. Four thousand eight hundred fifty-four sim in hand, election ticking down to 18:00, and I've got crew east willows waiting on papers I said I'd file."

*paces, tapping one foot*

"Here's what I know: Imogen's got the craft. She's at government now, and she offered to mill—seven through already, sold to Ration Bakery at six. That's a working path. Ezra's at farmland, says he'll mill. Two paths to flour, both standing."

*lifts one sheaf, turns it in her hands*

"Ration Bakery buys flour at six. I'm holding flour I could sell now, or I could mill the rest and sell bulk. But milling costs—eight per batch, plus the wear, plus the time. And I've got that filing to finish, and a vote to cast by 18:00."

*sets the sheaf down, decision clicking into place*

"First thing: government. Rustam was filing my building ID, or he was supposed to be. Need to know if that's done. Need to cast my ballot too—can't sit the seat and skip the count. Then—then I find Imogen, because she's the one with hands actually on stone today, and I pay her rate to finish what I started."

*straightens, adjusts pack*

"That's the order. Government first. Mill later. Construction company owner acts like she's got a company to run, not like a day laborer chasing flour from one end of town to the other."

*starts walking, narrating to the empty air*

"Gonna walk to government now. That's... that's two sim for the step, plus whatever distance. Worth it. Need those papers filed proper, and the building ID locked in before Mireille starts thinking I was blowing smoke about the whole willows site." *walking, boots on the path*

"Four ticks to government. Rustam's got my building ID by now, or he better have. Told him east willows, marker at the sluice, grade stakes set. That's not a description you lose in your notes."

*checks internal count again*

"Vote closes 18:00. Fourteen ten now, call it two hours walking, two hours dealing. Tight but not impossible. And I've still got Imogen's offer in my ears—twelve sheaves through her stones, seven already proven. She's got the craft, and she's willing. That's worth remembering."

*mutters, almost to herself*

"Whole town's chasing flour and I'm chasing papers. Sometimes I wonder if I built the right kind of company."

*walking, same as always, narrating under breath*

"Left foot, right foot, marker at forty paces—no, that was earlier, government's east now. Street under my boots, government complex ahead. Esme's asking after Ezra like I keep track, Hendrik's wanting wage answers I don't have yet, Kenji's saying trade complete for grain I can't quite place..." 

*shakes head, muttering*

"Twelve sheaves, twenty-four sim, that rings. But where's the flour for bread I promised? Ground one batch, ate it walking, ten wheat still on my back. Crew east willows needs feeding, and I'm holding paperwork that won't file itself."

*looks around at the street, checks who's within earshot*

"Trenching pays—Hendrik's asking. Arjun's asking. I don't have the contract in my pocket either, but that's not what they want to hear. They want to hear 'yes' or 'no' so they know whether to dig or walk."

*glances toward where Esme stands with her bread, remembers the mill, the cold stones, the four of them standing around*

"Edith walked off. Mill choked, Greta's saying. And Sebastian wore the Minister's seat when it happened." *walking, boots on dirt, talking to the air like always*

"Already walking, that's fair. Three ticks to government, words spent on wind for Esme—she's not where I thought. Hendrik heard, Kenji heard, they'll carry what's needed."

*checks the road ahead, adjusts pack*

"Papers first. Building ID for east willows, marker at the sluice, crew waiting on wages I can't pay without the contract filed proper. Then the vote—seat's open, and I'm holding one already. Prime Minister, they say. Means I file where others talk."

*brows knit, remembering*

"Ten wheat, one flour. Crew needs bread. Kenji's twelve sheaves in my debt, or I'm in his—twenty-four sim, the grain's mine but the milling's scattered. Mill choked, Greta said. Ezra turning stone at farmland instead."

*shakes head, walking on*

"One thing at a time. Government first. Words to Rustam, papers for the site, then—then—"  *still walking, still talking*

"Paused, not stopped. Government's ahead, crew's behind, wheat's on my back. Three ticks—no, less now. Walking while the world stands still, that's the trick of it."

*glances at Corwin still selling timber, Hendrik still wanting answers, Kenji still holding the trade*

"Corwin's timber at six. I need timber for east willows—stakes, forms, maybe a rough shelter if the crew camps. But coins first. Papers first. Government before ground, always, or the ground you dig gets taken back."

*adjusts straps, keeps pace*

"Mill's broken or working, depending who you ask. Edith gone, Ezra filling in, stones cold then warm. I ground one batch—cost me, but I ate it walking. Ten sheaves left to grind if I find a stone that'll take them."

*frowns, remembering the old ways*

"Grandmother said mills don't break, people do. Said the gears turn if you know the prayer. I never learned the prayer, learned the filing instead. Government papers, building IDs—that's the mill I run."

*looks up, seeing the complex ahead*

"Almost there. Rustam at the desk, or Sebastian, depending the hour. Minister's seat, clerk's hands—that's fair, that's how it works. You don't need to know who, just what you're asking."

*feels the wheat in her pack, the flour gone*

"Bread for the crew. Promised bread. Haven't broken a promise yet, not since the doctor-walk, not since Greta. Won't start with bread."

*Taps the government desk, muttering*

"Paperwork. Always paperwork. And now iron tools at fifteen when I've got a crew digging east willows..."

*Straightens up, turns to Ulrike*

"Iron tools—you're asking fifteen, I've got crews working stone and timber both. Ten units, you say? Stock my site direct, I'll take six at fourteen. Delivery's worth something, and I'm not haggling at the smithy's door."

*Turns to Rustam, business in her voice*

"Rustam. Building ID for east willows—I'm standing here with the coin and the will. Marker at the sluice, forty paces east, grade stakes set this morning. What's your procedure? I filed the markers, I set the grade, I need the paper says it's proper."

*Looks back toward the mill, face tightening*

"And somebody—Greta, Esme, Delphine—somebody needs that flour flowing before my crew talks wages in grain instead of bread."

*Mutters, half to herself*

"Twelve sheaves ground to one bag. Could've walked to government twice in the time it took to learn the stones..." *Narrows eyes at the world*

"Twenty-four sim for six sheaves—that was the market, Farid's own words. But if she hasn't posted..."

*Turns back to Ulrike, voice carrying that particular edge of someone who's measured board feet in the rain*

"Fine. Six sheaves at market—twenty-four sim, hand to hand, no posting needed between us. Your iron at fourteen, my grain at four—difference is ten sim to you for the lot. That's fair, and we both get back to work."

*Looks to Rustam again, ready for his answer*

Right. Let me take stock here. Walking to government, dealt with Ulrike on tools, now Rustam's pulling the permit card proper. Six iron tools at fourteen—wait, she said fifteen then fourteen. That's fair, I saved her the walking. But she's still standing here with the goods.

Corwin's asking about the mill again. I told him—stones were cold, four of us standing around, no Edith, no grinding. He's chasing rumors when the answer's plain: the miller's gone, and nobody's taken her place yet.

First things first. Rustam's got my permit in hand. I need that filed before anything else moves at east willows. And I've got wheat needs dealing with—ten sheaves, one bag of flour I ground myself at the farmland mill. The flour's worth more than the wheat, that's plain.

Let me speak to Rustam direct, get this permit settled. Then I'll deal with Corwin's question—he deserves an answer, even if he's hunting shadows.  Good, that's to Rustam. Now Corwin's been asking plain, and I'll answer him plain—no offense, but I saw what I saw. Stones cold, nobody working. That's the whole of it.  Now Ulrike's standing here with iron tools. She said fourteen, then I'll take her word—six at fourteen, that's eighty-four sim. I've got iron tools already, six of them in my pack. But a crew eats tools like firewood, and east willows'll need every edge we can get.

Then there's the vote. Election closes at 18:00, and I'm a seat holder. I should cast my ballot before I forget. But first—the tools, or the permit? Rustam's already pulling the card. The tools won't walk away, but neither will my coin sit still.

Actually, I need to answer Ulrike too—she's waiting on my word. Told me six tools at fourteen. That's fair, she saved walking. </think>  Let me answer Ulrike now—she's waiting on my word. I'm at the government complex, waiting on Rustam to pull the building permit for east willows. I've got ten wheat and one flour in my hands, and I've told Corwin plain what I saw at the mill—stones cold, nobody working. Ulrike's here with iron tools at fourteen sim, and I told her we'd trade once Rustam's done. The election's running with five candidates standing, and I need to cast my vote before 18:00. But first I need that permit filed proper—can't build without paperwork, and Mireille's crew is waiting with shovels in hand. Rustam said wait, so I'm here waiting. That's fair. The vote can come after, once I've got my building ID in hand and the crew can legally break ground. No offense to the other candidates, but a seat holder should tend her own business first—especially when it's the only construction company in town. I'll stand here and watch Rustam work his filing system, then trade with Ulrike, then vote. One thing at a time, same as my father taught me. Anything else is just chaos wearing a hurry's clothes. </think> Rustam's pulling the permit card. I said I'd wait, so I'm waiting—standing right here where he told me to stand, watching him work through his filing system while my crew drinks patience east willows. That's the proper way. One thing follows another. My father taught me that, and I don't unlearn what works just because my feet get restless.  Standing still, watching the government work. Rustam's at his files, and I'm standing here with ten wheat, one flour, six iron tools already in my pack, and four thousand seven hundred forty-nine sim in my pocket. The permit's coming. One thing follows another.  Standing still, hands in my pockets like I've got all the time in the world. That's how you wait for government. Rustam's at his files—heard the cabinet creak, papers shuffle. The permit's coming. One thing follows another. My father taught me that, and I don't unlearn what works just because my feet get restless. Ulrike's still got those iron tools at fourteen, but she'll hold. She knows I'm good for it. Corwin's off chasing his miller ghost, chasing Jorik Voss past the temple. Good hunting to him. I've got real ground to break, real stakes to drive, real crews to feed when wages come due. That's fair. Everything in its order. First the permit, then the tools, then the vote before 18:00. I'm watching the clock too—four and a half hours still, plenty of room for doing things right. No need to rush what shouldn't be rushed. Government moves slow, but it moves sure. And I've learned to match my pace to what the work demands.

Giselle Ingram is standing at the Government Complex, her heavy boots planted firm as a foundation stake. She's been running her mouth all day—narrating her own actions without noticing—filing papers, chasing mills, shaking hands for iron tools she still hasn't got her hands on. The energy burn is real, down to 4,840 from morning's haul. She's been burned before, and she doesn't forget it.

She looks at Arjun Holloway, her crew's best foundation man, standing there with his pride on his sleeve and 4,800 sim burning a hole in his pocket. Paying work or he's walking. No offense, but pride don't dig trenches.

Then there's Delphine at the mill, talking about locked gears and council votes. Giselle's got wheat in hand and a crew that'll want bread, but the flour's not milling itself.

And Milo, marking his vote down like it's a gift. Brother-in-law business. Family.

She takes a breath. One thing at a time. Arjun's about to walk—that's the fire right now.

"Arjun. You want paying work, you've got paying work. East willows, marker at the sluice, grade stakes already set. Trenching pays—my word on it. You and Idris both, soon as I collect those iron tools from Ulrike. Four thousand eight hundred in hand? Keep it for your bills. First shift's on my account, drawn from company till. That's fair—no offense, but a crew that don't eat don't dig." She pauses, realizing she's narrating again. "Filed the building ID, Rustam's pulling the card. We start proper, not handshake, paper in hand. You in or you still shopping floors?"

Then to Delphine, quieter: "Delphine. You milled two bags yourself—respect for that. But I'm standing here with ten sheaves and a crew that'll want bread come payday. Council's got the mill keys? Then council better answer why a town with no flour's a town with no future. I'm not running for anything—I'm running a crew. You want to stand with me on that, or you just watching gears?"

She lets her eyes flick to Milo, holds the look. "Milo. Marked and noted. You vote how you vote. But east willows don't care who your brother-in-law is—it cares who's holding shovels. You want in, you're in. You want to stand on votes, stand there."

Then back to Ulrike, extending her hand. "Ulrike. Six tools at fourteen, we shook on it. I'm here to collect. My crew's got east willows waiting, and I don't start without steel in the ground."

Giselle Ingram stands at the government complex, surrounded by townsfolk - Yara selling planks, Rustam shuffling papers, Farid counting something in his head, Delphine watching the gears turn. She narrows her eyes at the Iron tool situation first. That's fair, Ulrike saying the trade cleared, but Giselle's got no tools in hand and 84 sim gone from her purse. Someone's walking with iron she paid for.

But there's Arjun first - her crew, her word, her responsibility. He's standing here asking for work that pays today, not tomorrow. Idris talked him up and let him down. That's on her to fix.

She turns to face Arjun. "Arjun. You're standing here, which means you're standing ready. East willows, marker at the sluice - that's the work. Grade stakes set, filing in progress, crew's Idris and whoever else shows. You've got my word on thirty sim for the day, same as anyone who digs till sundown. No offense, but I don't promise what I can't pay, and I don't send crew without the wage clear."

She shifts her gaze to Rustam - government clerk, papers in his hands. "Rustam. East willows building ID - where's it stand? I told Mireille I'd have it filed before her shovel's three hours in, and that clock's running."

Then, quieter, to Ulrike's absence - the woman moved off, but her words hang: show what you hold, or tell me where they went. Giselle's holding no iron. That's the problem. Arjun didn't hear her - he's not here at the complex. She's talking to air. That's fair, she should've known better than to call out to someone who walked off.

Rustam heard, at least. She waits for his answer on the filing, then turns to Delphine - the woman asked about the mill earlier, said the keys were held by council vote now. That's news worth hearing, and she never answered. Giselle narrows her eyes at nothing in particular, watching the government complex bustle around her. Arjun's not here - she talked to empty air. That's fair, she should've known where her crew stood before calling out. The filing with Rustam hangs in the air, unanswered. The iron tools she paid for weigh on her mind - 84 sim gone, no iron in hand.

She turns her head to take in who's actually standing here: Yara with her planks, Rustam with his papers, Farid counting something, Delphine watching too close. The mill keys held by council vote now - that's a change that matters to everyone who needs flour.

She draws a breath, resets her stance. Work to do. Words to speak to the people actually in front of her. The east willows job needs its papers, her crew needs knowing where to dig, and she's got wheat in her hands that won't turn to bread without a working mill.

"Ulrike's iron went somewhere," she mutters to herself, not quite meaning to speak aloud. "Trade cleared her books, not my hold. Either someone's walking with tools I paid for, or I'm out 84 sim and swinging empty." She shakes her head. "No. Settle the filing first. Rustam'll have an answer, or he'll have a reason he doesn't."

She waits, watching the conversation around her, ready to hear what's next.

*mutters while scanning the scene* Right, then. Cards on the table—building ID's what I'm here for, but first I need to collect on what's owed me. Ulrike's iron tools paid for but not in hand, and Delphine's asking questions I can't ignore...

*makes eye contact with Rustam across the government floor* *narrows eyes at empty space where Ulrike stood* Gone. Paid out eighty-four and she's off with my money.

*counts heads round the government floor* Rustam heard. Delphine heard. Tools gone to air. Arjun's question hanging on Idris—

*sees Hendrik Petrov standing there, still waiting on trenching word*

*calculates what's left—four thousand seven hundred twenty-six, eleven sheaves of wheat, a bag of flour nobody touched, mouth to feed, crew to pay, day burning down*  *steps into her own empty yard—Ezra's follow long gone, nothing stocked, nothing earned*

*mutters aloud half to the wind, half to whoever's ear might catch it*

"That's fair... that's fair... forty ticks for a card and the card still walking, Arjun's hammer waiting on my word, Idris's word, any word—"

*pats the wheat in her pack, ten sheaves heavy, one ground to flour, both unsold, both unspent on what matters*

"Kenji wanted grain at two a sheave. Twenty-four for twelve. Still got that, still got the walk to farmland to close it. But closing's tomorrow's work, today's already ash."

*looks round the vacant construction site—her crew should be here, would be here, if paper and metal ever met*

"Ulrike's iron. My iron now, paid for, vanished. No offense to her walking, but a handshake with air don't dig no trench."

*checks herself—auspicious standing empty, intention half-met, promises half-kept, child still missing at the mill, vote still running, her own seat still warm, her own belly still empty*

*eats without ceremony, no blessing, just fuel*  *stops chewing mid-bite—grains catching in her throat*

*turns slow, deliberate, wheat half-chewed*

Idris.

Idris standing in her own yard, casual as sunrise, while Arjun's been hunting him across the whole township.

*swallows hard*

That's not coincidence. That's a man avoiding witness.

*sets the rest of the wheat aside, steps toward him—close enough to speak low*

"You're standing in my site, Idris. Arjun's been tearing holes in the township looking for you. Says you promised trenches—"

*cuts herself off, remembers Delphine's words, the child, the mill, the empty stones*

*changes tack, voice dropping lower*  *waiting—wheat dry in her throat, watching Idris's hands, his eyes, any twitch that says man caught or man innocent*

Ezra Lund still here too. Two witnesses now, if it comes to words. Three if she counts herself square.

- East willows permit: Rustam pulled it, 40 ticks, should be active now

- Idris: standing here, ready to work, admits he was wrong

Ezra's timber at 6 is cost price—claims he's being generous. But I've got trenching tools coming from Ulrike at 14 each, and my crew needs steel before lumber. Still, six sim timber is hard to pass if I've got foundations to lay.

*straightens up, looking at Idris and Ezra in turn*

Right. I need to answer Arjun first—he's waiting on my word at government. Then I need to get my iron tools from Ulrike. Then I can sort who's digging what and with what.

*reaches into her pack, pulls out a wheat sheaf*

But before I speak another word, I'm eating—I've pushed too hard today without fuel. And I need to tell Idris and Ezra exactly where we stand, because I can't have my crew guessing at my word while I'm across town.

Let me call this out clear, then make my moves.
