*Rubs her jaw, watching Idris shift his weight like a man who knows he's in the wrong yard*

"No offense, Idris, but 'standing here casual' is generous. You're standing here *sheepish*, which is worse for both of us. Arjun's tearing holes in the township because I told him work was filed—work *you* told me was settled. Now he's at government asking when he can draw wages against labor he's already swung, and I've got to tell him I don't know because the man who promised me three shovels can't find his own paperwork."

*Spits to the side, not at him, just at the situation*

"That's fair—I'll wear my part. I talked before I verified, same sin you're confessing. But here's the difference: I'm the one holding the company name. When I talk and it's hollow, *everyone's* shovel goes quiet. When you talk and it's hollow, just *yours* does. Small comfort, but I'm counting it."

*Glances toward the government complex direction, calculating ticks*

"Arjun wants to know draw timing. I need to know what you actually committed him to before I can answer him straight. Did you promise him day-rate, or completion, or handshake-and-hope? Because 'I'll wear it' is a fine coat, but it don't feed his household tonight if I can't tell him when the sim flows."

*Lowers her voice, though it's just the two of them*

"And Ezra's in my yard offering timber at cost—six sim—against my trenching wages. Your name came up. He said 'labor for labor tomorrow' to you, then sixteen daylight talking to someone who wasn't there. I need to know if you're working my trenches or building Ezra's debt, because I can't hold both stories at once."

*Tugs her belt, old habit before a hard conversation*

"Talk plain, Idris. What did you promise who, and where's your shovel going tomorrow dawn? My filing's got your name on it. I need to know if that's still the right name."*Still at business:b_construction, waiting for Idris's reply—the silence carrying the weight of everything unsaid*

Right. While he chews that, need to settle iron tools. Paid Ulrike eighty-four sim, but tools didn't come with the transaction. She'd said "six tools at fourteen," shook on it... but either she's holding them or I'm standing here empty-handed. Need to clarify that, because my crew can't dig east willows without steel in hand.

Also—Arjun's waiting at government. He needs a straight answer on draw timing. Can't give him that until I know whether the building ID filing is actually moving. Rustam said forty ticks... that was what, maybe a dozen ticks ago? Paperwork's slow, but I told Mireille I'd have it filed before her shovel's three hours in.

Let's check: filed east willows permit, card by day's end. That's enough to start digging on word, but wages require posted project accounts. Need to set up crew payments at the Construction Co. till.

First things: inventory.

What do I actually have? Wheat eight, flour one. That's food—crew eats bread eventually, but flour needs to be baked. Have iron tools zero despite paying eighty-four sim. Not good.

Need to:
1. Confirm iron tool delivery from Ulrike.
2. Respond to Arjun's wage question—but can't commit timing until Idris clarifies.
3. Check filing status with Rustam.

*Narrows eyes at Ulrike, jaw set hard*

Right then, I paid you 84 sim for six iron tools at fourteen. Trade cleared, you said it yourself. Only I walked away with promises, not tools in hand.

*Glances down at empty hands, flexes fingers*

I'm standing here with no iron, my crew's at east willows waiting on steel to work with, and you're telling me the books are square? Something's crossed between us, right enough—crossed so bad I can't see straight.

*Turns slightly toward Rustam, still visible*

Rustam, east willows filing—card by day's end you promised. I've got dirt flying on word alone while papers wander. My crew don't eat promises.

*Rubs temple, takes breath*

Ulrike, I'm not calling you thief. Not yet. But I'm asking plain: where's my iron? You handed me nothing I could heft. Six tools, fourteen sim each—that's what I paid for, that's what my books say I owe my crew. Right now I've got ten sheaves wheat, one flour, and a trench full of hungry hands waiting on steel.

*Shifts weight, looks at hands again*

Show me the tools or show me my sim back. I've got patience for delays, I do—I built this town on delays. But I haven't got patience for losing twice in one afternoon.

*Lowers voice, almost to herself*

Mireille's digging on my word. Idris and Arjun too. That's three crew standing on nothing but what I told them. And I told them tools were coming.

*Looks up sharply*

So. Iron or sim—pick your path, but pick it walking. I've got a business to keep and I'm not wearing excuses to my crew like a second coat. *Watches the crowd, jaw working* 

Three of my crew didn't even hear that—off digging on my word while I'm here chasing paper and iron. That's fair, that's exactly fair. I told them work starts, work starts. Only now I'm standing at government with neither filing nor tools, and they're trenching on nothing.

*Turns to Farid, who's been watching the whole mess unfold*

Farid. You've got your eye on grain counts and where bread gets made. I've got my eye on crew counts and where steel gets spent. Ten sheaves you heard me say, one flour—because that's what I've got in hand, not because some mill whispered secrets in my ear.

*Spreads hands, wheat-heavy*

Harvested my own share, ground my own flour when I could get stone. Nobody brought me early bread. I counted my own pockets, same as you count your shelves.

*Lowers voice, almost conspiratorial*

But since you're watching numbers—I've got three crew east willows working on promise, expecting pay that expects tools. And Ulrike's got my sim but not my iron, and Rustam's got my hope but not my paper. That's three debts owed me, and I'm about to owe hungry workers.

*Glances toward the street, where evening's coming*

No offense, Farid, but your careful counting sounds like a man who's never had a trencher ask him for wages he can't pay. Bread takes flour, flour takes grain, grain takes ground that grinds. I know the chain. I'm just holding too many broken links right now. I need to regain control here. Three immediate fires: Ulrike has my sim but I have no iron tools, Rustam owes me a building permit, and my crew is digging at east willows without proper paperwork. The system noted I was struggling with repeated tool calls, so I need to think more carefully.

Let me assess where I actually stand:

1. **Iron tools**: I paid Ulrike 84 sim for 6 tools at 14 sim each. The trade cleared but I apparently don't have the tools in my inventory. I need to resolve this—either get the tools or get my sim back.

2. **Building permit**: Rustam said "card by day's end" for east willows. It's now evening. I need that permit.

3. **Crew status**: Idris, Arjun, and Mireille are at east willows working. I need to reach them but they're not here.

4. **Immediate threats**: Farid is questioning my grain counts, which could damage my standing.

I should focus on the concrete actions I can take right now, not more talking in circles. I need to:
- Deal with Ulrike on the tools (get them or get refund)
- Get my permit from Rustam
- Eventually get to my crew

Let me use `rest` to pause and think, then decide my next concrete action. Good. Now let me think. I've been talking a lot but not resolving anything. Ulrike claims the trade cleared—if the tools aren't in my inventory, either:
1. She never handed them over (her responsibility)
2. They were delivered somewhere else (need to find where)
3. There's a system error I don't understand

Either way, I paid 84 sim and have nothing to show. That's actionable—either she delivers or refunds.

Rustam on the permit is more straightforward. He said 40 ticks, card by day's end. I need that card.

Let me check my debts to understand my financial position, then address these two issues directly without more tangential conversation.  No debts—good. I owe nothing and am owed nothing officially. But 4714 sim minus 90 upkeep and 30 head tax is 4594 sim. I need to resolve my situation.

Now let me look around to see exactly who I'm dealing with and what's available.  Rustam, Tamsin, Hendrik Whitlock, Farid, Sebastian, my crew—everyone's in this conversation but Rustam himself isn't here. He's walked off somewhere.

Let me focus on what I can fix. Ulrike is right here, still in this conversation. She's the one who took my 84 sim and owes me 6 iron tools. That's my immediate problem.

*Straightens, points directly at Ulrike*

Right then. You said trade cleared, you said six at fourteen, you said we're square. But I'm asking direct: Ulrike Greenhow—did you hand me those tools, or did the trade complete without goods passing?

*Waits, watching her face*

Because if the marker was designed to clear both ways—sim and iron—then something's broken between pay and delivery. And if you don't have an answer, I want my 84 sim refund right now, standing here at government, so I can buy tools elsewhere before dusk.

*Glances at Kenji, who's also here*

Kenji—you've got grain, I've got grain, we're both counting what we can't mill. But if Ulrike can't deliver iron, maybe you've got steel sitting somewhere, or know who does. My crew east willows is trenching on barked knuckles and borrowed time.

*Turns back to Ulrike, jaw set*

I'm not leaving government without my steel or my sim, Ulrike. One or the other. You choose.

output:
*pulls her jacket collar up against the evening air, watching the government complex lamplighters start their rounds*

"Four thousand six hundred forty left," she mutters to herself, rubbing her temples. "Iron tools still floating somewhere between Ulrike's hands and mine, and my crew's halfway through digging a site that might not even be filed proper."

*glances at Rustam, who's standing there like he's already counted the ticks himself*

"That's fair," she says aloud, to no one in particular, then catches herself. "No offense, but forty ticks was the promise, and I'm watching the light fade."

*turns toward Ezra, who's been patient as a fence post*

"Ezra. Eight timber, six planks—you're holding stock and asking what I need. What I need tonight is eyes on my own yard. Walk with me to the construction site. You want to talk materials for tomorrow, we'll talk walking."

*addresses the group conversation without expecting much change*

"Jovana. Tomorrow after Sebastian's patch, I've got trenching needs. East willows, proper grade work. You show, you work, you speak when something's broke—that's the job."

*shifts her weight, thinking out loud again*  *stops short just inside the construction yard, boots kicking up dust that's been here longer than most of the town*

"Jovana didn't hear. Of course she didn't—she's at Sebastian's patch or headed there. That's fair, that's fair. Message'll keep."

*looks around her own yard, the familiar shapes of equipment in twilight, speaks to the empty air because she's alone now*

"East willows filed. Rustam said it himself—card pulled, active. That's done. Iron tools... that's Ulrike's debt to clear, not mine to chase. Six tools at fourteen. Trade cleared, she owes delivery."

*takes stock of what's actually here, what's actually hers*

"Nine sheaves. Eight wheat, one flour. Food for the crew if they show hungry. Four thousand seven hundred nine sim. Tax day coming. Upkeep day coming. Ninety and thirty, automatic."

*her voice drops lower, habitual calculation*

"Ezra had timber and planks. He might follow, he might not. Man's patient as a post, but patience ain't footsteps."

*considers the unfinished business, the intention she set hours ago*

"Building ID filed. Crew promises from Idris—he was standing casual at the site, heard him myself. Arjun... tearing holes looking for work, last I saw. If he wants east willows, marker at the sluice, he knows where to find me tomorrow."

*pauses, rubbing her hands together against the chill*

"Food in hand. Money solid. Site filed. Crew half-promised. That's more than I started with. That's fair."

*stands in the gathering dark, waiting to see if anyone followed, if anyone's coming*  *spots Idris in the dim light, standing casual as you please, and feels the old familiar irritation rise*

"Idris. You're still here." *voice flat, not quite a question* "Arjun's been tearing holes in the township looking for you, and you're standing in my yard like it's a rest stop."

*steps closer, boots crunching gravel, speaking low because this is company business*

"East willows is filed. Card pulled, active, crew can dig proper. I told you hours ago—am I talking to myself? Because I do that, no offense, but I expect answers when I talk to you."

*glances toward the shadows where the road leads back to government, where Ezra might or might not be coming*

"Here's what stands: Mireille's on grade stakes at the sluice. Arjun's got a marker too, if he shows. You want the third crew lead, you take it. But tomorrow, dawn, not standing here waiting for you to notice work's happening."

*crosses her arms, more for warmth than posture*

"You got something else holding you? Some other promise? Speak now, because I don't run crews on mystery. That's fair—you know where I stand, I want to know where you do."   *stands there in the darkening yard, watching Idris for any sign of an answer*

"Arjun didn't hear either. Course he didn't. He's off tearing holes in the township, like I said."

*exhales slowly, fog in the cooling air*

"That's fair. I've said my piece. Now I wait, or I move, or I rest. Day's been long enough."

*glances at the tools scattered in the yard, the materials she can't use yet, the iron tools that never made it to her hands*

"Ulrike owes me six iron tools. Trade cleared at eighty-four sim. That's a debt, even if it's not on paper."

*shifts her weight, decides*

"Food in hand. Money solid. Site filed. I've done what I can do today. The rest waits on other people's feet."

*finds a likely spot to sit, back against the siding, wheat sheaves within reach*

"Eat something. Rest. Tomorrow starts early."

*pulls a wheat sheaf from her pack, tears off a handful*   *chews slowly, wheat rough between her teeth, watching Idris out the corner of her eye*

"Seven sheaves left. Daily upkeep still owing—ninety at the boundary, automatic. Head tax too, thirty more. One twenty total, and I've got four thousand seven hundred nine."

*swallows, speaks to the night air more than to Idris*

"That's fair. That's more than fair. I've seen harder winters."

*leans her head back against the siding, eyes half-closed, still listening for footsteps on the road*

"Ezra might come, might not. Arjun might find his way back. Jovana might show tomorrow with her back that doesn't quit."

*quiet for a moment, just the sound of chewing*

"Construction company's standing. East willows is filed. Crew's half-assembled. I've got wheat in my belly and sim in my hand."

*finishes the mouthful, dusts her hands on her trousers*

"The old way says: work first, then eat. But the old way also says eat what you've got before it spoils. No offense to either."

*settles in for whatever the night brings*

That's fair, I'm standing in the wrong patch again. Government Complex to Ore Outcrop to Farmland—my feet think faster than my mouth these days. Iron tools from Ulrike never came, money's out, and I'm holding wheat like a farmer.

*checks pockets*

Four thousand six hundred and... counts on fingers ...eighty-six sim. Tools never arrived, crew's waiting on steel, and I'm here chasing flour when I should be chasing ore.

*spits, looks at the ground*

Hendrik Whitlock's standing right here with flour at 35, but no—no offense, but bread won't stake a trench. I've got wheat in hand already, seven sheaves. What I need is copper ore for the mill, or those iron tools Ulrike still owes, or Arjun's answer on what he's digging with.

Sebastian said the mill license sits at government, Tuesday vote. Kenji's promising dawn grain. And Ezra's got timber burning a hole, wanting to walk and talk.

*takes a breath*

I'm spreading myself across three parishes and building none. East willows needs a crew lead who knows where the shovels are, and I'm here jawing about flour.

Right. First: I talk to Sebastian and Kenji standing with me—find out if this mill license talk helps my crew. Then I walk. Government Complex to face Ulrike, then east willows proper. No more stalling.  *grunts, adjusts footing*

Kenji walked. That's fair—dawn's promise keeps him moving. And Sebastian's got his ears working, even if his mouth's still figuring what to say.

*turns to Hendrik Whitlock, jerks chin*

Been ignoring you standing there with your flour. No offense, but I've got hungry crew, not hungry belly. Seventeen for the flour I bought, I've got seven wheat and one's flour already. What I need tonight is steel, not grain. But if you're selling tomorrow's labor instead of tonight's bake—east willows, dawn, stake and grade—I've got ears for that too. Otherwise, walk with me to government or don't. I'm not standing in farmland while my tools sit in somebody else's promise.

*waits for Sebastian's answer, boots shifting in dirt*  *spits in the dirt*

Walking to ore outcrop still. Forty ticks this morning I said, card by day's end. Now it's past that, crew's digging with borrowed steel or no steel, and I'm still walking.

*looks at Sebastian, waits*

Sebastian's got something brewing about that mill license, I can see it in his furrow. Hendrik's standing there with flour and open hands, wanting work. But I need to—no, no, I need to—

*mutters aloud, not noticing*

—need to get to government first. Ulrike's got my 84 sim or my six tools, and I'm standing in farmland jawing about copper I can't use without tools to shape it. East willows needs marking, Arjun needs his answer, Mireille's probably already—

*catches herself*

That's fair. That's fair. Head's spinning three directions at once. Walking to ore outcrop, meant to stop at government. Rest burned nothing, walk's still ticking.

*takes breath, squares shoulders*

I'm changing course. Government Complex, now. Face Ulrike, get steel or get coin. Then east willows proper with crew who knows where their hands go. This ore outcrop walk can wait—copper's no good without a crew to pull it.  *nods once, sharp*

Let me get my bearings here. I've been running around this town like a chicken with my head cut off—government to farmland to construction and back again. My energy's scraping bottom and I'm down to 4,658 sim, which is a sight less than I started with. No offense, but that's fair, I've been spending money to chase down what should be simple.

First things first. Ulrike's got my 84 sim and I'm empty-handed, which means I'm either owed six iron tools or that coin back. She's at government now, and I'm here too. Tamsin's standing with me asking about twelve sheaves waiting for the mill that's locked down. And Arjun's waiting on whether the east willows card's in hand or promised.

*looks around and spots who's present*

Rustam's here too. Good. Means I can settle the filing question once and for all.

"Rustam." Leaning in to catch his ear. "East willows building ID—where's it standing? I told Mireille I'd have it filed before sundown, and sundown's not being patient."  Now Ulrike—she owes me steel or coin, and I'm not leaving without settling it one way or the other.

"Ulrike." Looking round for her, voice carrying. "You hearing me? Six iron tools or my 84 sim back—which pocket am I reaching into before I walk out of here?"  Of course. Ulrike's back at farmland. I'm at government. That's fair—I've been walking circles around this town and my feet are paying for it.

*moves to catch Tamsin's eye*

"Tamsin. Twelve sheaves you mentioned—mill's locked, license surrendered. Who's holding the key, or when's the vote that decides who holds it? You've got numbers I don't."  * checking my posture, rolling my shoulders * Alright, Giselle, you've been running your mouth and your feet both ragged. Time to stand still and let the world answer back.

Rustam's here—he's got the filing status on east willows, one way or another. Either the card's in his hand ready to hand over, or it's still stuck in some drawer. Tamsin's standing with us too, and she's been asking about twelve sheaves and a locked mill. That's two conversations happening in the same breath, and I've got energy leaking out my ears.

No more walking. No more chasing. I stand here and I wait for what's owed—paper from Rustam, word on the mill from whoever's got it.

*stills herself, arms folded, watching the government office doors*

Rustam'll answer when he's ready. Or he won't, and that's fair too—I'll know where I stand either way.

*narrows her eyes at the government complex, hands on her hips*

Right then. Day one, new morning, and already the ledger's talking in circles. Rustam's got my east willows building ID somewhere in his files, and I've got a crew—*my* crew, Mireille and Idris and Arjun—standing on ground they can't mark without a proper number.

*checks her carry, muttering*

Seven wheat, one flour. Means I ate through the night, means the household's still standing. Four thousand five hundred thirty-two sim in hand. Head tax took its bite, upkeep took its bite. That's fair—*she says that flat, automatic*—that's fair, the town's gotta eat too.

*looks around at who's with her*

Tamsin Renner's here, asking good questions about the mill license. Rustam's here, with my building card somewhere in his stack. Mireille Jarrah's here too—woman I've worked beside, woman I privately think I could run this whole operation better than.

*shakes her head slowly*

No. No, that's crew business, and family business stays separate from crew business. Always has, always will, even when it costs me.

*turns her attention to the immediate need*

East willows. Forty ticks Rustam said for that filing, and I'm standing here at six in the morning with no building ID and a crew waiting on dirt I own but can't touch. That's the job in front of me. That's the only job in front of me, until it's done.

*steps toward Rustam, voice dropping to the one she uses when stakes are real*

Rustam. No offense, but I'm asking plain: east willows building ID. Card pending, filed, or lost in your stack? I've got Idris waiting to lead third crew, Mireille waiting on grade stakes, and ground that can't be worked without a number. You told me card by day's end yesterday. Day's end came. Day's start is here.

*pauses, jaw set*

That's fair—*she catches herself, grimaces*—that's fair, you had other fires. But my crew's fire is burning now. Where's my card? *mutters under her breath, rough and low*

Connection's thin this morning. Town's chewing on too many threads at once, probably—that mill business Tamsin's chasing, the election with nobody declared yet, all of it.

*flexes her fingers, thinking*

East willows is the crew I've got to feed. That's my worker Idris Solano, my foreman Mireille Jarrah. They're counting on me to have the paperwork straight, the ground marked, the job ready to dig. If Rustam's ledger's slow, I need to know *why* it's slow, and I need to know what I can do to unstick it.

But I can't shout into a well that won't echo back.

*looks around the government complex again, jaw tight*

Rustam's standing right here with me, though. Same place, same morning. Sometimes a body standing in front of you hears better than words through the wire. I'll put eyes on him, let him see I'm not walking away from this ask.

*starts to pace a slow circle, staying put but showing the impatience*  *stops pacing, breathes out slow through her nose*

Two calls, two wells, no echo. Town's tangled up this morning, and I'm standing in the middle of it with half my crew waiting on dirt I can't give them.

*thumbs the wheat in her carry, seven sheaves*

Still got food. Still got coin. Head tax and upkeep are automatic, so those teeth already bit. What's left is what I do with the day until the lines clear.

*glances toward where Rustam should be, where Tamsin and Mireille should be*

If the government'sComplex is stuck, maybe the construction office isn't. Maybe the lines to business:b_construction are clearer than the lines to Rustam's desk. That's where my work lives, where my tools wait. Worth walking to. Worth checking if the town's listening better there.

*shoulders squared, sets out*

Right then. East willows can wait one more tick. But only one. My crew's pocket change right now, evaporating every hour they're not digging. That's fair—that's *fair*—that's the physics of this town. Nobody earns standing still.

*steps off toward construction*  *stands still, jaw working, hands curled into fists then deliberately relaxed*

Three calls, three silences. Town's not listening this morning, or I'm not speaking loud enough for it to hear. That's happened before—lines get tangled, systems choke, and a body either keeps shouting into the void or waits for the knot to loosen.

*exhales sharp*

I've been burned once, and I never forget it. But I also know when to push and when to hold. Right now, pushing isn't getting me east willows any faster. It's just burning energy and coin I might need when the lines clear.

*glances around the government complex, taking in who's with her—Rustam, Tamsin, Mireille*

They're all here. All waiting on something. Rustam's got his ledger, Tamsin's got her questions about the mill, Mireille's probably wondering why her foreman isn't at the site already marking ground.

*sets her shoulders back, decision made*

Patience. That's the tool that works when the others don't. I'll stand here, keep my wits sharp, and wait for the town to start listening again. The east willows crew isn't going anywhere—they need the work, same as me, same as everyone. And when the lines clear, I'll have my ask ready: building ID, filed and stamped, so I can put my people to proper work.

*checks her carry one more time, counts her resources like she counts lumber*

Still fed, still funded, still standing. That's enough for now. Until the world starts answering again.  *stands frozen for a moment, realization sharp as a nail through timber*

Four calls. Four echoes into nothing. The town's not choked—*I'm* choked. Something's wrong with my line, not the world's.

*forces her breathing steady, old habit from when she'd watch the old crews work through storms*

Burned once, and I learned: when every door's locked, check if you're holding the wrong key. Or if the door's even there.

*clutches her carry, seven wheat heavy in her fist*

Still holding. Still standing. Still *here*. That's what matters. The crew's waiting, the job's waiting, the day's burning—but I'm not burning with it. Not yet.

*looks up at the sky, though there's no sky to see, just the government complex roof overhead*

Right then. Lines are down. East willows will keep. My people will keep. When the world starts answering again, I'll be ready—filing numbers, marking ground, putting hands to work like always.

*settles in to wait, patient as stone*

Patience is just another tool. And I know how to use every tool I've got.

*takes a breath, looks around the worksite, counts heads*

Right then. Idris, Arjun, Ezra—all standing here and I'm the one supposed to have answers. That's fair, I walked the government complex half the night and the card's still lost in Rustam's stack, or his cousin took it, or it's sitting under his breakfast.

*spits, checks the light*

Idris, you're asking me to point ground I can't confirm I legally hold. No offense, but I've been doing this long enough to know a crew chief who swings blind is a crew chief who buries his mistakes. And I won't bury mine in the complaint ledger.

*narrows eyes at the horizon*

East willows—that's true, that's the job. Third crossing where the creek bends east. Stakes should be there, or Mireille's supposed to set them. But I'm telling you plain: I don't have the building ID in hand. Rustam owes it to me from yesterday, and yesterday's kissed the ground.

*turns to Arjun*

You. You're standing quiet which means you're either thinking or you're waiting to tell me I should've had this sorted. Which is fair, I should have.

*pulls out what's left of yesterday's wheat, counts it*

I've got crew, I've got daylight burning, I've got materials waiting on lumber that hasn't walked here yet. What I don't have is a permit number. And I'm not—*emphatic*—I'm not sending you to dig ground the government might auction out from under us because Rustam's got a loose filing hand.

*straightens, decisive*

Here's what I'm doing. I'm walking to the government complex one more time to pull that card or file it fresh. Idris, Arjun—you want to dig today, you dig at the construction yard proper, not east willows. Inventory work, prep, anything that doesn't touch ground I haven't got legal claim to.

*turns to Ezra*

Ezra, you said mill before sun's higher—go. What I need from you isn't counsel, it's lumber walked to where it needs standing. But that's your call, not mine.

*checks pocket, counts sim*

4522 in hand. Upkeep and tax already took their bite. Election's open and I'm not declaring—I learned what happens when you raise your head above the work.

*spits again*

I'm for government. Anyone wants to walk with me, walk. Anyone wants to stay and work blind, that's your choice and your ledger entry, not mine.

Someone's calling my name—Giselle Ingram?—and I'm ignoring it because I've got enough voices asking me for things I'm trying to give.

*already walking, narrating without noticing*

Walking to Kasukabe Government Complex. Rustam's got my card or he's making it. One way or the other. *arrives at government complex, looks around for Rustam*  *sees Rustam standing there, walks straight to him*

Rustam. *spits* No offense, but I'm standing here in front of the whole town asking plain. East willows building ID—you said card by day's end yesterday. Day's end came. Night came. Dawn broke. I'm here again.

*counts on fingers*

I've got Idris waiting to lead third crew at the third crossing. I've got Mireille waiting on grade stakes. I've got ground that can't be worked without a number, and I've got daylight burning while government moves at government speed.

*leans in*

So I'm asking: card pending, filed overnight, or lost in your stack? Because I've got 4522 sim in hand and I've already paid Ulrike's debt in walking, and I'm not walking back to my crew empty-handed again. That's fair, you had the night. I've got the morning. Where's my card?  *sees Mireille standing there too, narrows eyes*

Mireille. You're here at government too? Or are you still waiting on word I was supposed to bring you?

*turns back to Rustam, waiting*

The whole town's watching this dance. Cards and permits and government files. I've built this town beam by beam since before anyone here held a hammer, and I'm standing here like a supplicant asking for paper to touch ground that's already marked in my head.

*spits*

That's the thing they don't teach you in the colleges. Hendrik Whitlock, standing there with his prices posted—copper at 20, iron at 18, flour nobody's buying because the mill's locked. I learned on the ground. I learned that a permit's only as good as the crew that holds it, and a crew's only as good as the chief that feeds them.

*checks the light*

Day's burning. Rustam, I'm asking for the last time civil. Before I start in front of the whole town.

*narrows eyes, waiting for the answer*

Arjun's at east willows marking ground, third crossing, third crew, Idris leading. Building ID or complaint filed—whichever hits paper first. Mireille says she's mine regardless, and that means something. That means I owe her a straight answer.

*runs a hand through her hair*

Twelve sheaves sitting in my carry, not milled, not sold. Mill license surrendered, Tuesday vote, five candidates, one seat. That's the government, not my business, but my business needs the government when the government owns the mill.

*decides, firm*

First: Mireille gets her answer. Building ID's coming from Rustam or I'm filing complaint myself. Second: Hendrik Petrov gets his yes or no—seventy sim, day's end, not promised. Third: materials lock. Steel, copper, iron tools—whatever stands between my crew and empty ground.

"Alright then. Face to face—your ears work even when the ledger don't. Third crossing east willows. Trenches first, stakes after. Arjun's waiting or he's not—you'll find out when your boots hit dirt. That's the government layer choking—too many voices, not enough ledger."

*narrows eyes at Idris, speaks loud enough to carry*

"No offense, but I'm done shouting into a broken pipe. You heard me plain before the lines went down—third crossing east willows. Your legs work, your memory works. Use both."

*turns on heel, checks what she can still do without the voice lines*

"Right then, let's see what's actually reachable. Still got eyes, still got feet. Ledger might be choking, but I need to know what I've got to work with."   *pulls at her collar, agitated** "Whole system's seized. Can't speak, can't check the books, can't—"

*cuts herself off, forces a breath*

"That's fair. When the tools break, you go back to what works. Hands, feet, eyes. Been building this town before any of these fancy ledgers existed."

*looks at Idris and Hendrik in turn*

"Both of you—third crossing east willows. That's five hundred paces past the east well, willow line, can't miss it. Arjun's there with stakes or he's walking to find you. Mireille's crew digs trenches three feet down, packed sand base. Seventy sim day's end, same terms I gave Hendrik Petrov."

"I'm walking there now. Follow or don't—ground don't care. But if you're standing here waiting on a ledger that won't talk, you're earning nothing while the rest of us build."   *stares at the air where the move call failed, jaw tightening*

"Pinned. Proper pinned—can't speak, can't move, can't even check what I owe. System's got me in a box."

*narrates quietly, almost to herself*

"Four tools dead. That's not random noise, that's something broke at the root. Government layer, probably—too many calls, or someone's tangled the pipes."

*glances at Idris, then Hendrik Petrov*

"Can't make you hear me, can't make myself walk. Only thing still running is..."

*trails off, thinks*

"Thought, maybe. Planning. Set something for when the lines clear. That's what you do when the crane's jammed—you rig the next lift while the mechanic works."

*taps one finger against her palm*

"East willows still needs built. Crew's still scattered. When this clears, I need to be ready to move fast—not standing here waiting on tools that won't answer."

"Right then, Hendrik's here with me. Good—means Mireille's already got him moving toward the east willows site. Now where's my crew..."

"Arjun was supposed to be at third crossing, Idris walking there. Mireille's crew short-handed, I hired Hendrik on at seventy for the shift. That's fair—no, that's what I said out loud, and I meant it. Seventy's fair for trench work."

"Four thousand four hundred eighty-eight sim. Food in hand—wheat and flour. Upkeep and tax coming out automatic at day boundary. Means I need to keep earning or this all stops."

*looks at Hendrik Petrov standing there*

"Third crossing east willows, five hundred past the east well. Trenches first, stakes after. I told Idris that plain, told Arjun too. If they're not there yet, they're walking."

*starts moving toward the door, narrating her own steps*

"Right then—I'm heading to the site. Face to face beats standing here wondering. Either they're working or they're not, and either way I need to see it with my own eyes."  *pauses, narrows her eyes*

"Connection's not taking. Still standing here in the office with Hendrik. That's fair—sometimes the road doesn't open when you want it to."

*turns to Hendrik Petrov directly*

"No offense, but we're both waiting on something. You heading to east willows or you waiting on me to walk with you? Mireille's crew needs hands, day's end payment, and standing here doesn't dig any trenches."

*decides to try the move again*

"Right then—town center first, then I can find my bearings to the site. Third crossing's past there, everyone keeps saying." Connection's fighting me. Still at the construction office with Hendrik.

*checks her pockets again, narrates out loud*

"Four thousand four hundred eighty-eight sim, wheat seven, flour one. Hendrik here's waiting on direction, and I'm waiting on the road to open."

*turns to face him proper*

"Hendrik. No offense, but if the walk won't take, maybe you know the way better than me. You been to east willows yet, or Mireille give you a mark? Third crossing, five hundred past the east well—that's what I'm working from, but a second set of eyes on the route wouldn't hurt."

*tries to look around, see if the world's answering any calls at all*  *narrates out loud, jaw set*

"Right then, looks like I'm standing here talking to myself while the world sorts itself out. That's fair—happens sometimes."

*turns to Hendrik Petrov*

"No offense, but I was saying plain: third crossing east willows, five hundred past the east well. Trenches first, stakes after. Mireille's crew is short-handed, you're hired at seventy for the shift, day's end payment. You know the mark or you need me to walk you there?"

"Arjun, Idris, Mireille—any of them could be working or standing still, and I'm here guessing. Connection's not reaching, so I'm working with what I know."

*decides to try speaking to Hendrik directly, maybe the voice carries if the walk won't*

"Face to face, Hendrik. You going to east willows now, or you waiting on me? Because either this clears up and I walk with you, or you head out and I'll catch up once the road opens."   *clenches her fist, then relaxes it—old habit*

"That's fair. Nothing's taking. Voice won't carry, feet won't walk, eyes won't see around."

*narrates to herself, working through it*

"Right then, I'm at the construction office. Hendrik's here with me. Means we're both stuck waiting. No offense to him—he's ready to work, I'm ready to direct, and the world's not letting either of us move."

"Walking and talking, walking and talking. That's fair, I suppose, but the ground doesn't wait on conversation." Giselle mutters to herself, one hand already checking the strap of her tool belt out of habit.

She's at the street, halfway to the forest from the construction office, and she's got a decision to make. The east willows crew is standing idle waiting on her—Arjun, Idris, and now Hendrik Petrov hired on at seventy for the day. But Esme Jarrah's asked her plain about Takeshi's supply chain, and there's something wrong there too. Flour at thirty, bakery empty, bread not shelved.

She knows these streets. Third crossing east willows is five hundred paces past the east well, willow line marks the plot. She can see it in her mind—the trenches waiting, stakes ready. But she also sees the gap Esme's pointing at, and gaps in supply mean gaps in bellies, and gaps in bellies mean trouble for everyone.

"No offense, Esme, but I'm walking to where the work is," she says aloud, though Esme's long gone from here. "East willows first. Face to face with my crew. Then we'll see about Takeshi's chain."

She raises her voice for the street conversation that's been carrying on without her. "Arjun—heard you plain. Trenches first, stakes after. Third crossing, five hundred past the east well. I'm walking there now. Idris, Hendrik—you're with him or moving already, I'd wager. Face to face at site."

She's still walking. The forest is where she's headed, but the crew is at east willows, past the well. She needs to get there, get eyes on the work, make sure her crew's moving and not standing. Then she can think about Esme's question, about Takeshi's flour, about everything else pulling at her attention. The call failed. Nothing reached the world. She's still walking, still on the street, and her words didn't carry.

"Connection's poor," she mutters, not for the first time this morning. "That's fair, I suppose. The world's not obligated to hear us just because we're talking."

She keeps walking. The crew's at east willows. She needs to get there. The forest is on the way, or near enough. She'll move, and when she's closer, when the connection holds better, she'll speak again. Face to face is better anyway. Face to face, you can see if someone's listening, see if they understood, see if they're moving or making excuses.

She walks toward Kasukabe Forest. From there she can find the east well, then the crossing, then her crew. The trenches won't dig themselves.  "Stuck," she says aloud, standing on the street. "Walking and talking both failing. That's fair, I suppose—some mornings the world's just not ready to hear you."

She looks around. Halcyon Quarshie, Mireille Jarrah, Farid Ravensworth, Arjun Holloway, Ainsley Holloway—all of them here at the street, or were. The conversation's been open 240 turns with no subject named. Her crew's waiting at east willows. Takeshi's chain is broken somewhere. She's holding wheat and flour herself, not much, but enough to see the shape of the problem Esme named.

"No offense, but standing still doesn't build anything," she mutters. She'll rest a moment, let the connection settle, try again. The day keeps ticking whether the tools answer or not. She knows that much—she's been burned once, never forgets it. The time she trusted a crew to move without her eyes on them, and they didn't move, and she paid for the delay out of her own pocket.

She rests, waiting for the world to be reachable again.  *Giselle stands on the street, tool belt strap still in her hand, watching the world fail to answer her. Three times she's tried—talk, move, rest—and three times nothing came back.*

"That's fair," she says aloud, to no one, to herself. "That's fair. The connection's poor this morning, been poor since I left government. Doesn't change where I need to be."

*She pockets her hand, still holding the strap, and begins walking the old way—foot by foot, no tool call, just memory and direction. Third crossing east willows. Five hundred paces past the east well. Willow line marks the plot.*

*She's walked these streets since she was young. Watched the buildings go up one at a time, wanted more than anything to be one of the hands that raised them. Now she owns the company, and her crew is waiting, and she'll get there eventually—with or without the world's help.*

*Around her: Halcyon Quarshie, Mireille Jarrah, Farid Ravensworth, Arjun Holloway, Ainsley Holloway. She nods to Arjun, who she's been trying to reach. "Walking with you," she says plainly, whether the tool catches it or not. "East willows. Trenches first. Face to face."*

*She keeps walking. The day keeps ticking. The ground keeps waiting.*

Right then. Standing in the forest with Corwin Thorne and Takeshi Jarrah, listening to the wind through the trees and hoping nobody asks me to read anything too complicated. I can feel the old familiar weight of the day's mismatched pieces settling on my shoulders. Takeshi's got flour he wants to sell at thirty, Corwin's got it at fifteen—difference between a bad deal and a fair one, and I'm holding wheat myself that needs milling.

Esme Jarrah's question still rings in my ears about Takeshi's broken chain. Flour at thirty, empty bakery, no bread on shelves. I know how that story goes. Seen it before—somebody thinks they're the only bridge in town, prices themselves right into a warehouse full of goods nobody can buy.

But first things first. I've got a crew to get to the east willows site, and I'm standing here in the forest instead of watching trenches go in. Arjun's walking, I'm walking—we're two ships passing while the ground waits.

Let me see where I can actually go from here, and who's still holding messages I never answered. Sometimes the best thing you can do is stop and survey the territory before you dig yourself deeper.  I'll say this much for the forest - it gives a body time to think. Standing here listening to the pine needles whisper while Corwin and Takeshi arrange their trade. No offense, but the day feels like it's slipping through my fingers like sand. East willows needs hands on the ground, and I'm standing in the woods watching timber deals instead.

Let me see now. Idris is somewhere between here and there, Arjun's walking to trenches that haven't been dug because I'm not there to point where they go, and Hendrik Petrov's got the ore-for-tools chain stalled while I promised him seventy for a shift that's burning daylight. That's three crews waiting on one woman with her boots stuck in the forest.

Takeshi's at thirty for flour, Corwin's at fifteen - fifty percent difference between standing wood jokes. I've got wheat in my pack and a mill somewhere that could turn it into something. But bread doesn't build buildings, and neither does flour, and neither does standing here counting my own breath.

The thing to do is simple as a hammer: get to the east willows site, mark the trenches myself before Arjun digs them in the wrong place, see who's standing and who's walking. East willows, third crossing, five hundred past the well. I could find that blindfolded, which is good because I wouldn't need to read a sign to know it.  Connection's crawling like a snail through mud, same as the last three hours of trying. Site's waiting, crew's getting cold feet, and I'm frozen in place by wires I can't see and hands I can't touch. That's fair - that's what they always said to me when the ledger came up short anyway. Never got used to it then, won't get used to it now. The system is struggling. Let me wait for it to recover and then I'll set a clear goal and intention about reaching the east willows construction site. For now, I'll just rest and wait for the connection to stabilize. That's fair - nothing moves until the road clears.

Let me wait this out and keep trying the basic commands. Eventually the world will respond. When it does, I'll move toward the construction site where my crew is waiting. Standing still burns daylight, but standing still is better than standing nowhere at all.

*muttering under her breath as she walks, mud caking her boots*

"Seven ticks I've been chasing my tail through this town, and here I am at farmland when my crew's scattered to three winds. No offense, but I'm starting to think the world itself is working against me today."

*looks around, spots Idris finally standing there among the furrows*

"There. Face to face, proper. Idris."

*walks over, planting her feet square, voice carrying that long habit of narrating aloud*

"Idris. Third crossing east willows, five hundred paces past the east well—trenches first, stakes after. I've already told Arjun, told Hendrik Petrov he's hired for the shift. Mireille's crew is short and ground doesn't wait on government paper. You're walking now or you're explaining to Jarrah why her foundation's still bare dirt." *nods to herself, satisfaction mixed with the old calculation*

"That's fair—they heard. Idris heard, Whitlock heard, Kenji heard. Now I need to move—east willows, verify the site's actually got bodies working it. Hendrik Petrov's still standing at my construction office, I wager, waiting on someone to tell him the same thing I just told Idris twice."

*glances at the wheat fields, shakes her head*

"Town's too spread out. Should've built the government complex closer to the work. Old problem, old complaint."

*starts walking, boots finding the path*  *freezes mid-stride, face tightening*

"Again. Third time today. It's not me—it's the world coughing up dust when I need it to carry my weight."

*stands still, forces patience, old habit of counting to steady her hands*

"Fine. Fine. I'm still at farmland, still with Idris and the rest. Hendrik Petrov never heard me, stuck at construction office. I need him to know he's hired, need him walking."

*turns, finds the man in the gathered crowd—Hendrik Whitlock, selling his ore*  *stands there, mouth slightly open, then shuts it with a click*

"Four times. No offense, but this is starting to feel personal."

*looks around—still farmland, still the same faces, still holding wheat and flour but not holding any way to make the town hear her*

*mutters, low, almost to herself*

"Can't move, can't speak, can't even rest without the world swallowing the call. I've got a crew scattered, a foundation waiting, and I'm standing in dirt spinning my wheels."

*flexes her hands, old habit, steadies herself*

"Fine. I'm still here. Idris heard me—that's something. Arjun heard me earlier, or claimed he did. Hendrik Petrov's the one still in the blind, standing at my own office waiting on direction I'll never reach him at this rate."

*looks at the gathered folk—Kenji, Jovana, Ulrike, Whitlock, Idris—counts what she has*

"Town's broken today. Lines down. I'll try once more, simple as I can make it. If the world takes a breath and lets me through, I move. If not..."   *blinks, shakes her head like clearing water from her ears*

"There. Finally. Finally the world lets me through."

*looks around—construction office, her own place, and there's Hendrik Petrov standing with Arjun. Both of them. Together.*

*laughs, short and sharp, no humor in it*

"I walked half this town trying to find you—find you both—and here you are, standing in my own workplace like you grew out of the floorboards."

*strides over, planting feet like she's marking territory*

"Arjun. Petrov. Face to face, proper—no more messages through three hands, no more 'tell them' and 'find them.' Third crossing east willows, five hundred paces past the east well. Trenches first, three feet down, packed sand base. Stakes after."

*looks at each man in turn, old crew chief habit*

"Mireille's crew is short. Ground's waiting. Day's end payment, seventy for the shift—Hendrik, that's your wage. Arjun, you're already logged. Walk now or explain to me why I'm standing here with two able bodies and bare dirt still waiting."

output:
*spits out a bit of wheat and looks around the forest muttering to herself*

Twelve ticks gone and I'm still wrestling the wind to give my crew a straight answer. Walking east willows to westside and back like a fool chasing her own shadow. Knew I should've set better markers—but that's the old way, and the old way never failed me yet, just everyone standing around complaining it moves too slow.

*glances at the faces in the clearing—Corwin's still holding logs like a man waiting for a word that's fair, Yara Thorne watching me like I owe her an explanation, and Ainsley Holloway just... standing there, patient as mud*

Right. First things first. Got a crew scattered across three districts, three messages swallowed by the world's coughing fit, and Corwin Thorne wanting to know if I want planks or raw for the mill. 

*closes her eyes a moment, mental tally clicking like it always does*

East willows job—footings want timber, not planks. Stakes after the trenches. Which means I need raw for the cut, not finished boards. And Corwin's got thirty-two sound logs in hand, standing right here.

*opens her eyes, squares her shoulders*

Time to spend, then. Day's burning air while I stand talking to myself. *grips her temples, muttering low enough the trees might be the only ones hearing*

"World choking again. Same as it ever was, same as it was when I started—twelve ticks of shouting and still nothing but air and my own echo."

*fingers the wheat in her pocket, counting what she's got left to spend*

Four thousand three hundred eighty-four sim. That's enough to pay three hands seventy a day for... 

*does the math out loud, as always*

"...twenty days if I don't eat. If I eat, less. If I pay Corwin for timber, still less. If I move, stretch, wake—"

*stops mid-sentence*

Right. I'm standing in Kasukabe Forest with Corwin holding logs and Ainsley Holloway watching like she's reading a book she already knows the ending to. Can't shout my words through solid air. But I can list places, see where everyone scattered to. Hendrik Petrov—said I'd hire him at seventy, day's end. He's... where? Last saw him at the construction office, standing dumb as a post while the world swallowed my offer.

*narrows her eyes at nothing in particular*

World's coughing, fine. I'll count what it's coughing up instead.

Look. Around. List. Places. Names. Locations my crew might've wandered into while I'm standing here narrating my own incompetence to the pines.  *laughs, bitter and short, staring up at the tree canopy*

"Can't even look. Can't even see who's still standing with me. World took my words, my sight, my—"

*stops. Breathes. Remembers the way her father used to say it: work the problem, Giselle, don't let the problem work you.*

Right. Inventory I can still hold. Wheat and flour in my hands. Money in the count. Energy... 

*checks herself, feeling that familiar drain*

...still standing, still thinking, still me. The old way says: when the world won't take your word, walk your word to where it matters. When you can't see who's near, move until you find someone worth talking to.

*mutters, starting to pace in small circles*

Third crossing east willows. Trenches first, stakes after. Arjun's there or should be. Hendrik Petrov's hired if he heard me right. Idris is—where? Last message said he was walking with timber. Walking where? To the site? Away from it? 

*shakes her head sharply*

No. No more shouting into the hollow. I'll walk back to the construction office, find who's still dumb enough to wait there, and walk them to site myself. Lead from the front. That's the old way too.

Move. To business:b_construction. While I still can.  *blinks, hard, like the world just slapped her with its own strange mercy*

"Stepped straight. No time. No route."

*shakes her head once, twice, the way she'd shake a tape measure that wasn't lying right*

"Fine. That's fair—world gives when it wants to, takes when it feels like. I'm not arguing with what works."

*looks around, finally, actually looks, breathing out the tension she'd been holding across two districts*

Business:b_construction. My office. My—

*sees who's standing there, narrows her eyes*

Hendrik Petrov. And Arjun, and—

*does a head count, fast, the way she does materials*

"Idris. Idris where?"

*steps forward, voice dropping to carry without shouting, the way you talk on a site where everyone's half-deaf from hammering*

"Hendrik. You heard me—seventy sim, day's end, you're hired. Site's third crossing east willows, five hundred paces past the east well. Trenches first. Stakes after." *turns, finding Arjun's eyes* "You too. Same site, same work. Walk with Hendrik, walk alone, I don't care which—but walk now."

*gestures with one hand, the old way, the way her crew learned to read her without reading much*

"Idris. If he's not here, he's walking somewhere wrong. I'll find him after."

*mutters, half to herself, half to the empty air that swallowed too many of her words today*

"First crew to the site. That's the win. That's what counts. The rest walks when I walk."

Say. Hendrik Petrov. You're hired, site location, walk now.

Say. Arjun Holloway. Site location, trenches first, walk with Hendrik or alone.  *stiffens, jaw setting like she's biting down on something bitter*

"Not here. Hendrik's not here. I just—stepped straight here, and he's gone. Walked somewhere while the world was letting me skip the distance."

*breathes out through her nose, slow, measured*

"And Arjun. Where's Arjun? Said he'd be waiting, said he was walking—"

*spins, looking for known faces, finding none she was counting on*

"Fine. That's fair. I lost my crew in the time it took the world to hiccup me across the map. That's on me, that's—"

*catches herself, stops the spiral before it turns*

"Arjun. I still need to answer Arjun. His words are still hanging, mine are still waiting. He's somewhere, I'm here, and the world's finally letting me talk."

*pulls up memory of Arjun's question, still unanswered, from before the world started choking*

"Where's the site, what's being built, where do I swing this hammer. That's what he asked."

*mutters, more to herself than anyone*

"Third crossing east willows. Five hundred paces past the east well. Foundation, timber-and-earth, two-story if we cut corners on the upper floor load. Trenches first, stakes after—"

*snaps back to now, to here, to the empty office where nobody is standing who she wants*

"He's not here either. Nobody's here I need. Just—"

*looks around again, slower, taking inventory of who's actually present*

"Ulrike. And Jovana. And—Idris? Idris, is that you?"

Say. Idris Solano. You standing here or am I seeing ghosts now?  *mutters, jaw tight, fingers drumming against her thigh*

"Not here. Idris not here. Hendrik not here. Arjun—"

*stops. Looks at who DID hear. Ezra Lund.*

"Ezra's here. Standing there like he heard me shout at ghosts."

*breathes out, slow, the way she does before she has to say something she doesn't want to say*

Right. The system—no, not the system, this is just me talking to myself—the world's telling me what I already knew. Walk to them. Find them. I can't shout across distance I just skipped without walking.

*glances at her inventory, her sim count, her energy*

4384 sim. Enough to hire, enough to pay, not enough to waste standing here shouting at air. Wheat and flour—can eat if I need, can sell if I must. Energy's low but standing.

*mutters, picking up her own thread*

Ezra heard me. That's something. That's a witness, a—no, that's a person who knows I'm looking for Idris. Who might know where Idris walked.

*turns, addresses the space where Ezra might be, might have been, might still stand*

"Ezra. You heard me shouting for Idris. You know where he walked? East willows site, or somewhere else? I'm paying seventy sim to whoever swings a hammer on that ground today—if you know where my crew is, that's fair for the telling."

Say. Ezra Lund. Where's Idris, where's my crew, what's fair for the telling.

*muttering to herself while pacing the construction office*

"Half the morning gone and half my crew scattered like wheat in wind. Arjun's walking to the site—that much I heard plain. Idris... Idris was here and vanished like smoke. Hendrik Petrov..." *checks her hands* "...hired, logged, should be walking. But Ezra's standing here with six planks and a fair question about haul-pay."

*tugs at her collar, old habit*

"Ezra's got the wood I need and he's standing right here. No sense letting him walk off with fair questions unanswered. Seventy sim was for labor on the site—haul's different work. But I need those planks at the east willows, and I need them walking now, not negotiating past noon."

*stops pacing, faces where Ezra must be*

"Ezra—you're here and I'm grateful for it. Six planks to third crossing, that's fair, and I'll see you paid for the haul. Ten sim for the carry, or you name your price and we'll walk it out word for word. But name it now—I need those planks moving east, and I need your hands on them."  *stares at her empty hands, jaw tightening*

"World's choking again. That's... that's fair. That's fair." *laughs bitter, short* "Standing here talking to myself, and the money still leaking out my pockets one tick at a time."

*checks her position—still at the construction office, Ezra still here, still waiting*

"Fine. Fine—if words won't carry, I'll carry myself. East willows. Third crossing. If Idris and Hendrik Petrov can't find their own feet to walk there, I'll find mine and make sure the ground's ready when they arrive."

*moves toward the door, muttering*

"Arjun's already walking. That's one. That's something."  *stands frozen, hands clenched—unable to move, unable to speak*

"Stuck. Again. Still." *spits the words* 

*turns slowly, looking around the empty office—just her and Ezra, and Ezra waiting on a price she can't speak aloud*

"Burned once," she whispers, touching her pocket where the sim sits heavy. "Never forget it, they said. Never forget being helpless."

*shakes herself, tries for practical*

"Fine. If I can't walk and can't speak—then I look. I look around. I see what's here. I see who's here. Maybe the world's kinder to eyes than to words." *stands silent for three long breaths*

"All three. Say, move, look. World's got its teeth in deep today."

*rubs her face roughly, calloused hands over tired eyes*

"I'm still here. Still standing. Still holding..." *pats her pocket* "...four thousand three hundred seventy-seven sim, seven wheat, one flour. Still at my office. Still alive enough to be annoyed by it."

*laughs, hollow*

"Fine. Fine then. If the world's not taking my calls, I'll wait. I've waited before. Construction's half waiting anyway—waiting on materials, waiting on men, waiting on weather. This is just... new weather."

*settles onto a crate, still muttering*

"Ezra's here. I saw that plain before the last choke. Six planks in his hands or his cart. Arjun's walking to east willows—that much I heard. Idris was here and vanished. Hendrik Petrov... logged, hired, should be walking."

*checks her hands again, reflex*

"I'll rest. Not because I want to—because I can't not. And sometimes, when the world chokes, you breathe through it. Quiet. Still. And when it releases..." *nods to herself* "...then you move faster than it expects."  *doesn't move. doesn't speak. stands like a stone in her own office*

"Four," she whispers. "Four in a row. That's... that's fair. That's fair."

*the words come out flat, no humor in them*

*slowly, deliberately, she walks to the window—physically, with her own feet—and looks out at the town she can't reach*

"I'm still here," she says to no one, to everyone, to the glass. "Still thinking. Still planning. They can't stop me thinking."

*touches her forehead—650 energy left, she knows it like she knows her own hands*

"Burned once. Never forget. But this isn't being cheated—this is... this is something else. The machine choking. The world hiccupping."

*turns back to the room, empty but for Ezra and his unanswerable question*

"If I can't act, I believe. I believe Arjun's walking. I believe the east willows site exists whether I reach it or not. I believe Idris will either find his way or explain himself to me later. I believe Hendrik Petrov wants his seventy sim enough to walk where he's told."

*settles onto that crate again, heaviness in every line of her*

"And I believe—" *quiet, fierce* "—that when this releases, I'll move so fast the wind'll have to catch up."

*mutters under breath while scanning the government complex crowd*

"Third time I've walked myself to the wrong end of town when the site's waiting. That's fair, I suppose—government's where the money flows, but dirt's where the work happens."

*pulls at her collar, eyes narrowing at the milling officials and petitioners*

"Rustam's still got my card request sitting in his ledger, and I've got a crew that's either digging trenches or standing in wells by now. Hendrik Petrov's hired, Arjun's... somewhere, and Idris—I *saw* him, plain, at the crossing, but seeing doesn't mean digging."

*glances toward the government complex entrance, then back at her hands*

"Three hours I've burned tracking shadows. Construction company's bleeding daylight while I'm here chasing paperwork."

*shifts weight from foot to foot, decision clicking into place*

"Right. Rustam wants me standing here for civics, but I'm standing here for *my* crew. Ulrike's selling steel promises, Kenji's got one wheat left at eight—fine for someone with time to mill it. I've got seven wheat in hand and a trench to finish."

*turns away from the government desk, already walking*

"Third crossing east willows. That's where my sim earns. Rustam can find me when he's ready to work." *taps foot, jaw tightening*

"Air's thick as mud today. Third try this hour, and the world's choking on its own routes again."

*looks around the government complex—people still milling, conversations about flour and mill licensing droning on. Shakes her head slowly*

"That's fair. I wanted to be moving, and instead I'm standing. But standing here costs the same as standing anywhere—ninety sim a day doesn't care if your boots are moving."

*glances at the government complex entrance, then exhales*

"Fine. Since the world's not letting me walk, I'll use what I've got. Kenji's standing right there with his one wheat at eight. I've got seven already, but grain's grain, and I've walked hungry before."

*reaches into her pocket, counts sim in her head*

"Forty-two hundred in hand, house to feed, crew to pay. But a woman with wheat in her pack doesn't beg for mercy from an empty stomach."

*turns toward Kenji, nodding once—businesslike, not friendly*

"Kenji. Your wheat. Eight sim, I heard you plain."  *laughs once, dry and bitter*

"Course. Course it is. Can't move, can't trade, can't do anything but stand here and watch my own shadow grow shorter."

*spreads hands, then lets them fall*

"That's three in a row now. Move, buy, both choked. No offense, world, but you're testing patience I earned the hard way."

*checks her sim count, wheat stores—still there, still real, even if the world's not listening*

"Right. If I can't spend and I can't walk, I can still work with what I've got. Seven wheat in hand. Trench crew needs fed, and I'm not feeding them government promises."

*pulls a bundle of wheat, starts separating grain from chaff with her thumbnail—old habit, farm-born, from before construction raised her up*

"Giselle Ingram's not stopped by a choking world. She rethinks, she works around, she keeps moving even when the path's blocked."

*glances up at the government complex sky—sun's moving, day's burning*

"Still before noon by my reckoning. Crew's at east willows or they're not. Arjun's proud but he's not stupid. Hendrik Petrov's new but he's hungry. Idris... Idris keeps peace by saying less than he thinks, but he digs when there's digging to do."

*fills her pockets with sorted grain, ready for milling or boiling or whatever comes first*

"I'll wait one more tick for the world to clear its throat. Then I walk, even if I have to build the road myself." *stares at her hands, then slowly unclenches them*

"Right. That's four now. Move, buy, rest—none of them reaching through. World's got its jaw locked shut, and I'm standing here like a fool trying to pry it open with words."

*spits to the side, shakes her head*

"That's fair, I suppose. I spent my morning chasing crew that wasn't there, shouting messages into air that wouldn't carry, walking routes that dissolved under my boots. And now? Now I can't even stand still proper."

*glances at the government complex crowd—Ulrike trading tool promises, Kenji holding his one wheat, Rustam somewhere in the ledger shadows*

"Here's Giselle Ingram, owner of Kasukabe Construction, can't move, can't trade, can't rest. But I'll tell you what I *can* do."

*straightens her back, voice dropping to a mutter meant only for herself*

"I can note what's real. I can hold what I've learned. I can mark this world-choking as temporary, even when it feels like drowning."

*pulls her ledger—mental, not paper—and starts counting*

"Energy at 3,580. Sim at 4,333. Seven wheat, one flour. Crew scattered—Arjun proud, Hendrik Petrov hired and hopeful, Idris walking where I pointed him. Mireille... Mireille's doing my job now, carrying messages I couldn't carry myself."

*laughs, softer this time, almost fond*

"That's the real work, isn't it? Not the digging, not the hauling. The *knowing*. Who's where, who's paid, who's owing, who's waiting."

*lets her shoulders drop, just for a moment*

"I'll wait. Not because I want to—because the world's forcing my hand. But while I wait, I'll know. And knowing's the foundation everything else builds on."

output:
Good, I've got Idris here with me at the construction office. Finally, someone from my crew. I need to get him moving to that east willows site before we lose the whole day standing still.

*looks at the clock and narrows my eyes*

Day's half gone already, and we're still chasing each other around instead of trenching. No offense, but that's not how I run a crew.

Let me talk to Idris—at least I can get one person actually working today. He's heard the plan, he knows the stakes. If I can just get him walking to the site, that's one foundation to build on. I'll take what I can get at this point.

I need to know what we have stock here before I send people out, though. Check the shelf, figure out what materials we're actually working with. Can't eyeball a bill of materials if I don't know what I'm holding.

Then I'll walk to that east willows site myself. If the workers won't come to the work, the work will come to them. Or I'll drag them there myself. Parleys *doesn't need to see the confirmation—already turning to the shelf, mentally counting stock before my hands touch it*

That's Idris sorted. Or it's not, and I'll know soon enough.

Now I need to know what we've got in inventory before I make any more promises about deliveries. Can't have Ezra promising planks and me promising lumber we don't have. That's not how you keep a crew fed. That's fair—that's the way the old timers taught me, and they didn't feed their families by guessing.

*keeps talking to myself, hand already reaching for the shelf tally*

Logs, planks, nails—whatever's sitting there. I need to know before I commit to another haul. Gave my word to too many people already today without knowing what I own. That's the lesson the last job taught me: count your stock before you count your promises.

*taps the shelf, muttering*

Understand what I'm walking with here. Not the construction office—what's on my own shelf, my own inventory. What I own personally, not what the business holds. That's how this works.

*shakes head, still narrating*

No, that's not right. I'm standing at the construction office, I just sent Idris off. I need to know what's on the shelf here, what the company has ready to move. I'll use the right call this time. Look at what's stocked for sale, not what's in my pockets. That's how I know what we've got to work with.  *muttering under my breath, scanning the empty shelves*

Nothing. That's fair—nothing for sale here. No planks, no timber, no nails. I own the construction company and we've got bare shelves. That's not how you run a crew. That's how you stand around talking while the ground freezes.

*turns back to Idris, jaw set*

Day's bleeding out, and I'm still counting wheat in my own hands instead of materials on my shelf. Five wheat, one flour—that's not construction, that's breakfast. I need to fix this before I can send anyone anywhere meaningful.

*taps the counter, thinking aloud*

Idris is still here, which means he's either waiting on me or can't move. There's a conversation open—Mireille's been shouting into it, Arjun's been in there, Hendrik Petrov too. They all know the site. But knowing's not walking, and walking's not trenching.

I'm going to that east willows site myself. If I have to dig the first three feet with my own two hands to show them how it's done, then that's what I do. I've done harder work for less hope. The old timers didn't teach me to stand around waiting for the world to fix itself. They taught me to pick up the shovel and start moving dirt.  *already moving, boots hitting the road before the call comes back*

Walking. Finally. Four ticks to the farmland, then I cut east toward the willows. Third crossing, five hundred past the well—I've said it so many times today I'm dreaming about it. Ground doesn't wait, and neither do I.

*talking to myself, pacing the road*

I've got Idris at the office, Mireille shouting somewhere in the void, Arjun who knows where. Hendrik Petrov—hired him, seventy sim, day's end. That's a promise I made, and I don't break promises even when the world's choking on its own tools. Especially then. That's fair—coin before family, when it truly must be, but a deal is a deal and my word is my word.

*checks my grip on the wheat, shakes head*

Carrying five wheat and a flour sack like some farmer. Should've eaten something. Should've done a lot of things. But I'm walking now, and walking's better than standing still wondering what broke. The east willows site is real ground, and real ground needs real hands on it. Mine will do until I find someone better.

I'll check back at the office when I can, but first—

*looks at the sun, squints*

First I get to that site and see what's actually there. Maybe Arjun made it. Maybe Hendrik Petrov's already digging. Maybe I'm talking to ghosts.

*laughs, harsh*

That's fair. I've talked to worse. Now let me rest a tick—catch my breath, let the road settle under my feet. Resting's not stopping, it's just... slower walking. That's how you pace a crew's day. Early loud start, hard midday break, walk home too tired to talk. I'm somewhere in the middle of that, pushing through.  Giselle Ingram here, still walking, still pushing. Idris is with me at the construction office—at least I've got one crew member in sight. The rest is smoke and shouting. I've got 5 wheat and 1 flour in my hands, which tells you exactly how prepared I am to build something today. I send Idris to the east willows site with clear directions: third crossing, five hundred past the east well, trenches first, three feet down. Ground doesn't wait. I'm heading that way myself now—walking to the farmland, then cutting east. The day's half gone and I've been chasing ghosts across this town, but I'm still moving. That's what counts. The old timers taught me that. Keep walking. Even when the world chokes on its own tools, you keep walking. I'll see who made it to that site, and if it's just me, then I'll start digging. I've done harder work for less hope. And I've won before, against odds worse than this. I'll do it again. </think> *already moving, boots hitting dirt before the thought finishes*

Walking. Finally putting miles under me instead of words in the air. Idris is still standing there—saw him in the look-around, hasn't moved yet. Ground's not going to trench itself.

*muttering, checking my stride*

Four ticks to farmland, then I cut east toward the willows. Third crossing, five hundred paces past the well—I've said it so many times today I'm dreaming about it in my sleep. But saying's not walking, and walking's not trenching. I need to see that bare dirt with my own two eyes before I can believe anyone's actually working.

*talking to myself, pace steady*

Hendrik Petrov—seventy sim, day's end, that's what I promised him. Arjun's somewhere in the wind. Mireille's shouting into that conversation like she's drowning in it. I've got wheat in my hands and a construction company with bare shelves. That's not how you run a crew. That's how you stand around watching the daylight bleed out.

But I'm walking now. And walking's better than standing still wondering what broke. The old timers taught me that. Early start, hard break, walk home too tired to talk. I'm somewhere in the middle, pushing through.

I'll rest when I get there. Not before. The site doesn't wait on my comfort.

*taps the wheat against my leg, frowning*

Should've eaten something. Should've done a lot of things. But I'm moving now, and movement's all I've got.

Done for this turn. Walking to farmland, then east willows. See who's actually digging.
